America isn't empty empty. Its population is still growing. Its cities remain raucous and crowded. Its suburbs are buzzing. But the country is starting to feel a little less full.
For years, economists and demographers have warned about the coming "Great People Shortage," a time when the US population would begin to decline thanks to lower birth rates and aging baby boomers. While the current situation is not yet as dire as those predictions, the ground is shifting in ways likely to reshape the American economy. The decrease in babies born years ago is now becoming more perceptible, as fewer people are reaching adulthood and joining the labor force. Plus, the Trump administration is giving America's ongoing demographic shifts a shove by making it harder for foreigners to enter the US, closing off one of the country's main buffers against a workforce that's getting smaller and older. Tourism is weakening, too, amid rising prices and hesitant international visitors.
The effects may not show up in the national head count yet. But the slowdown will start to appear in the places and industries that depend on a churn of newcomers.
The US population isn't expected to fall off a cliff soon: The Congressional Budget Office expects the number of people living in America to peak at 364 million in 2056 before it starts to decline. But in a country where the fertility rate crested in 2007 and isn't likely to go back up anytime soon, there are a lot of unanswered questions lurking underneath that topline number — namely, will there be enough working-age people in the places that need them to power the economy?
Immigration has historically been a crucial part of the answer. The last few years have seen some wild swings in the country's net international migration. Under the Biden administration, it ballooned to 2.7 million in 2024, per the Census Bureau. It fell to 1.3 million in 2025 and is expected to decline to 321,000 in 2026. In terms of the workforce, that's a big deal.
"Immigration is usually about half our job growth," says Pia Orrenius, a labor economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas. When fewer immigrants arrive, it becomes harder for employers to fill jobs, especially in regions that need workers. That means lower output, slower growth, and less demand, because immigrants aren't just workers, they're also consumers. Orrenius points to Texas, which is in the midst of a manufacturing boom and building out data centers. "If you have a stagnant economy anyway that doesn't really grow much or really generate a lot of new jobs anyway, you're not really going to feel it as much," she says. In Texas, however, "we grow fast, and we depend on immigrants and migrants from other states to fuel that growth."
While incoming immigration numbers have waxed and waned over the decades, America is in novel territory regarding its broader attitude toward foreigners already in the country. Not only has the White House undertaken mass deportation efforts and cracked down severely on entrances at the border, but it has also revoked thousands of visas for students and workers and ended protections for hundreds of thousands of people living in the US from countries such as Venezuela and Haiti. Whether they're a white-collar tech engineer or a blue-collar roofer, non-natives across the economic spectrum are less welcome in the US.
Immigrants don't simply take jobs that would otherwise go to US-born workers. The two groups often do different, complementary work. Immigrants also create demand — they buy groceries, rent apartments, and start businesses that fuel local economies.
Fewer tourists from abroad impact economies, too. Many foreigners have decided to avoid Stateside visits under the Trump administration. The president's antagonistic stance toward Canada and ongoing tensions with our neighbors to the north has resulted in a steep decline in visitors from there. Tourism from Europe and Asia has fallen.
People are just a little less footloose.
Leigh Barnes, the North America president of Intrepid Travel, an international travel company, tells me they've seen a 67% decline in Canadians traveling to the US from 2025 to 2026, a 30% decline in inbound visitors from Australia and New Zealand, and a 24% decrease from Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. He attributes the drop-offs to a mix of politics and economics. Canadians have had a "visceral" response to Trump's stance toward their home country, while visitors from Australia and the United Kingdom, for example, are more put off by financial pressures at home and increased costs in the US. Once tourists arrive in the US, he says they often discover "everyone's bloody lovely," but the problem is that they're nervous about getting here. "It's that trepidation and concern coming into the border," he says.
The cumulative effect is an uneven demographic era. There will be some places with fewer workers and some places that continue to grow. Attractions and cities that depend on international tourism will take a hit, whereas others that don't get many visitors won't see a difference. Some colleges will survive the drop in international students, navigate a world with lower attendance, or successfully entice enough young people to enroll. Others will struggle to weather the storm.
The competition for an increasingly scarce number of young people is also complicated by the fact that Americans are moving less than they once did, says William Frey, a demographer and senior fellow at Brookings Metro. "People are just a little less footloose," he says.
The result will be more parts of the country emptying out, especially rural areas that don't have the same kinds of job opportunities they used to have. They can't offer the jobs and amenities more populated areas do.
One thing that is true across the country: the population is aging. "That's probably a bigger, broader concern," Frey says. Baby boomers are exiting the workforce, and there aren't enough young workers to backfill them, take their jobs, and replace their tax dollars. This is also changing the nature of jobs the country needs — someone has to care for these older people.
For up-and-coming American workers, this setting isn't necessarily terrible news, says Steven Ruggles, a regents professor of history at the University of Minnesota. Workers entering the workforce in 2040 — about 15 years down the road — will have a "pretty darn good" labor market, he says.
Companies will have to compete for the available workforce, which will mean greater leverage, stronger job prospects, and higher pay. "When the baby boomers entered the labor market, the labor unions disintegrated because they no longer had any bargaining power because workers were a dime a dozen," he says. On the flip side, it also means companies will try to squeeze more out of every worker they can hire. "If there's a shortage of workers, you expect there to be a lot of incentive for companies to adopt labor-saving devices like AI and other things that increase productivity," Ruggles says.
One thing that's hard to know is how sticky current conditions are. The slowing of immigration under Trump isn't permanent, just like the explosion under Biden wasn't. Once America's political winds change, policies around green cards, student visas, and immigration enforcement are likely to change. Tourism may bounce back. Low birth rates and an aging population are less likely to change.
America's future depends on how and whether the country adjusts to an older, less mobile population — and how leaders think about filling the gaps.

'A lie' & 'nonsense' - Palmer committed to England, says Rogers
- Published
Morgan Rogers says any suggestion Cole Palmer is not committed to England "is a lie" and "nonsense".
Rogers scored the opener in Wednesday's 2-1 Uefa Nations League win over Croatia, with Harry Kane adding a penalty on his record-breaking 126th appearance for the men's side.
But his Chelsea team-mate, and childhood friend, Palmer had been left out of the squad after boss Thomas Tuchel said he "misses too many chances to impress".
The 24-year-old Palmer, who was also not called up for the World Cup, withdrew from the previous England camp in September citing a minor injury.
Forward Rogers, also 24, was asked about the criticism of Palmer following the win at Wembley, and told BBC Radio 5 Live: "He wants to be here.
"He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done.
"He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself.
"But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 or 15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it.
"It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. It's a lie.
"You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it."
- Is Palmer's England career over under Tuchel? 
  - Published6 days ago
- A must pick or unreliable? Tuchel's Palmer dilemma 
  - Published5 November
Struggles under Tuchel
In the three years since his England debut, Palmer has only won 14 caps, scoring two goals - including one in the Euro 2024 final defeat by Spain - and having one assist.
That is despite scoring 50 Premier League goals with 24 assists.
He was named England's men's player of the year for the 2023-24 season after some impressive form, including his strike against Spain in the Berlin showpiece.
But Palmer has only featured in three of Tuchel's 27 games since he succeeded Gareth Southgate as manager.
Some sketchy form last season, though, meant the former Manchester City player missed out on the the summer World Cup, with England going on to finish third after losing to Argentina in the semi-final.
He was named in Tuchel's first squad after that, but withdrew despite having played in all Chelsea's league games to that point.
Tuchel said this week: "We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together.
"I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.
"We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress."
But the German added: "It's not personal. We will never assume Cole is in the mindset never to come to the camp.
"Cole is always in our mindset but the competition is on."
Bellingham an example to follow
Palmer should not give up hope of getting back into Tuchel's good books.
Last October Jude Bellingham was left out of the squad for a friendly against Wales and a World Cup qualifier against Latvia.
The Real Madrid midfielder then ended up being a key part of the England team at the World Cup, scoring seven goals.
Former Three Lions goalkeeper Paul Robinson added on BBC Radio 5 Live: "You can see what Thomas Tuchel is doing when you look at what he's done with Jude Bellingham.
"It was only 12 months or so that Jude Bellingham was getting left out of an England squad. Jude Bellingham was getting left out of England starting XIs.
"Call it what you want, but it was management from Thomas Tuchel to make Jude Bellingham realise that he wasn't the lone star of this team. The team was the star. The team was better with Jude Bellingham in it, playing at his highest level.
"There was a lesson in his management skills with Jude Bellingham and I wouldn't be surprised if he's doing the same now."

To say that Olivia Benson and Elliot Stabler have a complicated relationship would be an understatement. During the Nov. 12 600th episode of “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit,” Benson (Mariska Hargitay) is forced to reopen a case that she worked with Stabler (Christopher Meloni) many years ago, realizing they likely put the wrong man behind bars.
After convincing him to come help her with the case, Benson learns that he had shut her out of the case and taken control, something she allowed him to do. But she’s the captain now — and isn’t going to allow their old patterns to return.
“I love that we got to push up against each other because that’s also family. There are so many feelings between Benson and Stabler. It’s so complicated — what could have been, what was, what we’ve shared, the ‘ride or die,'” says Hargitay. “People ask, ‘Why do you think people love Benson and Stabler?’ And it’s because of their dedication to each other, their trust in each other.”
Since Stabler “was so formative in her development as a detective,” this episode highlighted how they move past that. “It’s about a woman having her voice,” she says. “So many women identify with that.”
Hargitay was excited to dive into such a strong storyline about the duo.
“I think that we also just wanted to tell a truthful, complex story that people could identify with, have big feelings about, and understand the complexities of these types of relationships, and give them something real to go up against,” she adds. “We are so focused on keeping it real and making it good, and we know that just by being together, the fans will be happy. That’s why we invited him back because we knew they’d be so happy, and that’s what they would want. But also, he’s such a big part of the story. It’s truthful to have him back at this juncture.”
At the end of the episode, Stabler invites Benson to take some time off and go away for a few days. The audience knows she has days off available, since it’s specifically mentioned early on, but that doesn’t mean she says yes. In fact, it was never even an option, says Hargitay.

The Telescope in Fisch lets players trigger powerful weather conditions, boosting their fishing progress at night. This effect is called ‘Astral Anomaly’, which helps you get high luck and a chance of getting mutated fish depending on the lens you use. However, you will first need to unlock the Telescope and collect all the required lenses. In this guide, we will tell you how Telescope works in Fisch.
How to Activate Telescope in Fisch
The Telescope is located in the laboratory. To access it, you first need to complete Astronomer Vega’s quests. You can find Astronomer Vega beside the large Telescope in front of the laboratory at coordinates -1878, 225, -414. You can use the Fisch GPS to locate him and start the questline:
- A Battery Dilemma: Obtain two Battery Casings for Astronomer Vega.
- Activating the Telescope: Complete any Anomaly Investigation quest.
This is the same location where you can unlock the Glimmersuit Speed Boots in Fisch, right outside Dr Crookspine’s office.
To find Battery Casings, you need to mine crystals inside any of the Astral Caverns; just make sure you have a pickaxe, and you are good to go. Once done, return to Astronomer Vega and complete the marked Anomaly investigation.
Head to the marked location in the Boreal Pines and talk to Brayden. Complete his small quest, and he will reward you with a Stellar Lens.
After completing these quests, you can interact with Astronomer Vega to use the Telescope.
How to Change Telescope Lens in Fisch
The Telescope uses different lenses to activate Astral Anomalies. Each Telescope Lens in Fisch triggers a specific anomaly during the night and provides a unique buff. Follow these steps to operate the Telescope:
- Talk to Astronomer Vega.
- Recharge your telescope by clicking on ‘Recharge’ below the battery.
- Select the number of Enchant Relics you need (each charge requires 1 Enchant Relic).
- Click on ‘Change Lens’ and choose a lens.
- Click on ‘Activate’ to trigger the Anomaly.
The standard battery just gives five charges; you can unlock the Reinforced Battery in Fisch and increase your Telescope’s charge to 20. When it runs out, using Enchant Relics tops the charge back up.
Fisch Astral Anomaly Effects and Buffs
You can change the Anomaly effects by swapping the lenses. Each lens gives you a different mutation in Fisch. Here are all five lenses along with their bonuses.
| Lens | Astral Anomaly | Buff | 
|---|---|---|
| Stellar Lens | Celestial Congregation | 2.25x Luck and 5% chance for Celestial mutation (4x) | 
| Seasonal Lens | Evershifting Eclipse | +25% XP and 5% chance for Solarblaze mutation (3.5x) | 
| Deep Lens | Abyssal Alignment | +20% Weight and 5% chance for Abyssal mutation (5.5x) | 
| Experimental Lens | Meteoric Outburst | Better meteor loot and 5% chance for Chaotic mutation (6.2x) | 
| Moonlit Lens | Lunar Eclipse | 5% chance for Lunar (2.5x), Celestial (4x), Nova (6x), and Aurora (6.5x) mutations | 
Each anomaly has a different use, so choose a lens based on the bonus needed for your fishing session.
That is how you unlock and use the Telescope in Fisch. Did you craft all the lenses yet? Let us know in the comments.

Sheinbaum rebuts Trump, says no migrant caravans have reached US border since January 2025
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum says no migrant caravans have reached the U.S. border since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025
MEXICO CITY -- Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said Thursday that no migrant caravans have reached the U.S. border since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025, responding to his threat to double tariffs on Mexican goods unless Mexico stops migrants from traveling through its territory.
“Not a single migrant caravan has reached the north” since January 2025, Sheinbaum said at her daily news briefing.
Sheinbaum said a caravan of about 600 migrants traveling through the southern state of Chiapas had largely dispersed after its members were told that reaching the United States would be “very difficult.”
She said Mexican authorities were also in talks with another group of several hundred Honduran migrants, encouraging them to return to their home country.
Asked whether Mexico would use force to break up the caravans, Sheinbaum ruled out such measures, saying authorities have “extensive experience” accompanying migrants and explaining that they have little chance of crossing into the United States.
Trump’s latest tariff threat comes as Mexico and the United States continue negotiations aimed at reducing or eliminating duties Washington imposed on several Mexican products last year.
The talks coincide with a review of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, or USMCA, which began in July.
Mexico is seeking significant reductions in the 10% tariffs imposed on Mexican goods not covered by the trade agreement, as well as the 25% duty on medium- and heavy-duty trucks.
Negotiations have also addressed a 50% tariff on steel and aluminum and a 17% countervailing duty on Mexican tomatoes.

For more than 30 years, the paper covered an increasingly repressive state under Vladimir Putin.
Novaya Gazeta was a newspaper of near-legendary status in Russia. It was the home of the investigative journalist Anna Politkovskaya, whose books in the early 2000s offered a searing account of human rights abuses, wartime propaganda and corruption in Vladimir Putin’s Russia. In 2006, on Putin’s birthday, Politkovskaya was shot and killed in the elevator of her apartment building. Twenty years later, Russia is back at war and Novaya Gazeta has shut down.
On Monday, the paper held its last editorial meeting. One final issue will come out in the next few weeks. I spoke to my colleague Valerie Hopkins, who was there to witness the journalists packing up their offices.
Sadness, defiance and pride
Valerie, Novaya Gazeta, the last big independent Russian media organization, closed its newsroom this week. The paper and its journalists have been under intense pressure from President Vladimir Putin for decades. Why now?
The real miracle is that they lasted this long. We’ve watched the Russian government systematically dismantle any media organization that is critical of the Kremlin and critical of the war in Ukraine. This didn’t happen overnight.
First their website was blocked, so you needed a VPN to read them. Then they lost their media license. Then Putin signed a decree nationalizing their printing presses. Then this spring, authorities raided the newsroom and one of their journalists was detained and put on trial. The paper was added to the list of so-called foreign agents — this kind of Stalin-era term that comes with many limitations on what you’re allowed to do.

LastWave, Musify, Convx, Spotube, and SimpMusic are free open-source clients for YouTube Music and Spotify. They unlock premium perks without subscription fees or ad tracking, offering background playback, offline downloads, time-synced lyrics, lossless audio, and customized interfaces without locked controls.
Subscription prices are going through the roof. And when you stack multiple subscriptions together, it can put a big hole in your pocket. For listening to music, we usually depend on Spotify and YouTube Music. They are the default music streaming sources for millions across the globe. Though there are alternatives from which you can hear high-quality audio, they just can’t match the ease of popular apps. But you are bombarded with ads, and several features are locked behind a paywall unless you pay.
Thankfully, you don’t have to search the internet for free options. Developers around the world have built free apps that give you many of those perks. Below are five of the best, what each does well, and what to watch out for before installing.

Why are open-source music apps worth a look?
To be clear, most of these apps are clients. This means that they don’t store any music themselves. They plug into a service like YouTube Music and show it in a cleaner, ad-free interface with extra features on top, which you’d usually get after paying for a premium subscription. For me, Spotify has been the go-to music streaming app, but slowly the app has become quite greedy.
After a few times, the next and previous song buttons get locked, and it asks you to pay to unlock them. I mean, what is wrong with companies today? Thankfully, I have now ditched Spotify and have picked one of the below open-source music options.

- No ads and no subscription fees. Everything below is free.
- Most of these apps have no ad trackers or tracking SDKs.
- New features are constantly added, and some of them aren’t even available in paid apps.

Best free open-source music apps
LastWave
If you care about how your music sounds, LastWave is the one to install first. It’s a free YouTube Music client for Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux. Most of us would care about the free music that we get with LastWave, but you will soon appreciate the quality of music that it offers. And since it is a YouTube Music client, you are getting access to almost every song that is available on YouTube.

On compatible phones and headphones, LastWave also plays the Dolby Atmos version of a song automatically. For those who own a USB DAC or a pair of IEMs, there’s a bit-perfect mode that sends raw, unprocessed audio straight to your device.

Musify is for people who just want to open an app, search for a song, and press play. It’s a lightweight Android app built around Material You, which means its colors automatically match your phone’s theme and wallpaper.
Using it is fairly easy. You search for songs, albums, artists, or playlists and start streaming over Wi-Fi or mobile data. If you want to save data or listen on a flight, you can download tracks and play them offline. It lets you create your own playlists, rename and reorder them, or import existing ones from online sources. The player shows lyrics so you can follow along. You can also control the quality of the audio.
There are no annoying banner ads, no audio ads, no sign-up, and no tracking inside the app, and the interface is translated into dozens of languages by the community. I found this to be a great choice for older phones, or for a parent or sibling who finds complicated apps annoying.
Convx
While most open source music apps work well, there are only a few that also feel nice to use. Convx comes in the second category. If you like iOS’s “Liquid Glass” design, then you would love Convx. It brings iPhone’s Liquid Glass design to Android, with frosted, see-through menus, floating controls, and album-inspired colors that change with whatever you are playing.
Under the pretty surface, Convx is a complete music player. You can browse and stream music, save songs for offline listening, build queues and playlists, set a sleep timer, change playback speed, and tweak the sound to your taste with an equalizer. What makes it stand out among the heavy hitters is its DJ-style playback. You also get automix, crossfade, and smooth transitions between one song and the next. Lyrics are synced word by word and come from several providers, plus it gets animated artwork.
Convx can play local files and even songs stored on a home server or NAS through SMB and WebDAV. You can choose the option to import your Spotify playlists, show what you’re playing on Discord, scrobble to Last.fm, recognize songs playing around you, and use Listen Together to sync playback with friends.
Spotube
Spotube is the veteran here, with over 46,000 stars on GitHub, and it works differently from the rest. Instead of being locked to one service like Spotify or YouTube, it runs on plugins. You choose your own music sources, metadata, and playlists through plugins made by the community, or if you’re good with it, you can write one yourself.
The biggest advantage is that it works everywhere. Spotube runs natively on Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux. This means you can use the same app on your phone and your laptop. It’s small, fast, and light on data. You can import and sync playlists from popular music services or manage them locally. It gives time-synced lyrics from public lyric databases no matter which source you use. Offline downloads are supported, with proper metadata and ID.
Privacy is one of the biggest highlights of Spotube. It collects no telemetry and no user data. Installing it is also easy, because you can download it through winget, Scoop, Chocolatey, Homebrew, Flatpak, and F-Droid.
SimpMusic
SimpMusic is that one app that does everything. It’s a free YouTube Music client for Android and desktop that borrows many of Spotify’s best ideas. You can play music from YouTube Music or regular YouTube without ads, and it gets you background playback. You can browse the home feed, charts, podcasts and moods, search everything on YouTube, cache songs for offline playback and use Android Auto.
SimpMusic Wrapped gives you a year-in-music recap just like Spotify’s. Then there is monthly recap playlists and listening charts that stay on your device. There are three Now Playing styles, including one that looks like Apple Music, and the lyrics are synced in 12 languages. You can even share lyrics as an image.
You can switch to 1080p video with subtitles, skip sponsor segments with SponsorBlock, see dislike counts with Return YouTube Dislike, and use a 10-band equalizer with AutoEq headphone profiles.
Which one should you pick?
If you care most about sound quality, I would suggest LastWave. If you want something simple, pick Musify. If design matters to you, try Convx. If you want plugins and an app that runs on every device you own, choose Spotube. If you want the most features in one place, install SimpMusic. The best part is that all five are free and can be installed side by side, so you can try a few and keep your favorite. You will get access to unlimited songs from the best sources in good quality. Let us know which one you chose, and comment below if you have a different app that you use for listening to music.

European nations are seeking an envoy to represent them in talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war, concerned that a U.S.-backed process will leave them sidelined as Moscow and Washington decide the fate of a conflict that has roiled the continent.
Whether that should be one individual or more, and who it might be, is being debated as leaders from the 27-nation European Union meet Friday (November 13, 2026) at a summit in Dublin. Senior EU officials and politicians have been suggested, but there is not yet a consensus.
What the job might entail is also unclear and contested. But there is broad agreement among governments from the U.K. to Ukraine on the need for Europe to join the ongoing negotiations involving Moscow, Kyiv and Washington.
Ukraine is eager for backup from its European allies, as it's reluctant to leave the talks solely in the hands of a U.S. administration that has often seemed to lean toward Moscow's views. Russia does not want European countries involved in direct negotiations, complaining they are financing and supplying Ukraine's military effort.
And the Europeans do not trust U.S. President Donald Trump to negotiate on their behalf after a series of tense standoffs over trade, Greenland and conflicts in Iran and Ukraine.
“Without Europeans, there is no support for Ukraine,” French President Emmanuel Macron said at the European Political Community meeting in Dublin. “There is no more U.S. support."
“At the end of the day, we will be the ones to define and decide for our future security as Europeans,” he said.
Europe is broadly aligned but not unified
European leaders fear Russian President Vladimir Putin will press Mr. Trump to back a peace settlement that weakens not just Ukraine but broader European security. Putin has demanded that NATO troops be pulled back from Russia's borders and that no European forces be deployed in Ukraine.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham rejected the idea that Europe was being sidelined during peace negotiations, saying “there are European voices in the room.”
“All the leaders I've spoken to today are determined to put a bit of a ring of steel around Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as part of all of this to back him up to the hilt, and that's what we will do,” he said.
As envoys from Washington, Moscow and Kyiv met in Abu Dhabi, several European countries, including the U.K., France and Germany, attended discussions nearby.
Supporters of a single envoy, like Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, argue that their absence has let individual countries or small groups engage in freelance diplomacy.
“There are too many different groupings discussing the issue,” she said.
Ms. Meloni has criticised a series of seemingly uncoordinated initiatives, including a call to Putin by Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, that she said could undermine European interests.
She has increasingly pushed the idea of a common EU representative to speak with “a single, authoritative voice” and has requested a decision by Friday (November 13) in Dublin to be formalised in December, in coordination with non-EU partners in Europe like Britain and Norway.
Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin said that “Europe has to have a coherent negotiating price at the table, but it's not just the European Union" and called for “a wider European continent perspective” that includes the U.K., Norway, Canada and others.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov argued that for Europe to join peace talks, it first must name a representative. “The Europeans squabble like spiders in a jar. If someone takes the initiative to establish contact with the Russian side, those people face ostracism.”
An old question with no clear answer
The question of who represents Europe is an old one. Europe itself is loosely defined. Is it the 27-nation EU, the 32-nation NATO military alliance made up mostly of European countries, the 29-nation Schengen zone, or the 47-nation European Political Community?
That has frustrated Washington in the past and present.
After this week's U.S.-brokered talks between Ukraine and Russia in the United Arab Emirates, envoy Jared Kushner said that “if Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiation.”
That echoes the famous quote attributed erroneously to former U.S. Secretary of State Henry Kissinger: “Who do I call if I want to call Europe?”
Potential candidates from within the EU
France, Germany and the U.K., the region's top three economies collectively known as the European trio or E3, have so far been the most engaged European body in negotiations. But while London is deeply involved with Ukraine, it left the EU in 2020.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday (November 13) that the E3 is “a proven format” for diplomacy.
But an E3 envoy would leave out the other 25 EU nations and rankle smaller nations like those that border Russia and Belarus on the bloc's “eastern flank” which face constant hybrid threats, including influence campaigns and disruptive drones.
Some back a top EU official for the job. Even inside Brussels, however, there are two leading contenders: European Council President Antonio Costa and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas.
Mr. Costa's current role is to represent national leaders. A former Prime Minister of Portugal, he spent much of the past year visiting capitals across the bloc.
“European security cannot be discussed without a European voice at the table,” Mr. Costa said in Dublin. “That European voice needs to be a team effort between European nations, the European Union and NATO.”
But earlier this year, Mr. Costa faced down criticism within the EU after his office set up a hush-hush backchannel with Moscow.
Ms. Kallas, a former Prime Minister of Estonia, could also lay claim to the position of envoy.
She said in Dublin that the E3 represents the “big countries” but then asked “who is representing the European Union?"
"Americans are representing American interests. Europeans are representing European interests,” Ms. Kallas said, adding that the EU's foundational treaties are “very, very clear” that she and Costa were appointed in 2024 to represent the bloc in “security matters.”
Ms. Kallas, however, has had a bumpy track record with U.S. diplomats as Washington and Brussels sparred over trade and Ukraine. She's also acknowledged issues between her office, the EU's External Action Service, and the Commission.
Another name that has been floated is Mr. Stubb, the Finnish president. He has warm relations with Mr. Trump and met in Oslo with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Mr. Kushner in October. A week after that, he called Mr. Putin with mr. Store, the Norwegian Prime Minister. Mr. Stubb spoke with Mr. Zelenskyy by phone on Tuesday (November 10).
Urgency is needed in Europe, said Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs, pointing to recent cyberattacks, arson and a drone attack in Leipzig, Germany.
“The threats are real," he said. "We're going to see more and more and more because that's the way how they can stop the support of Ukraine. That's what they want to achieve.”

Barely two months after rival upGrad acquired Unacademy, cofounder Gaurav Munjal is now stepping down as the chief executive officer (CEO) of the test prep platform. In a post on LinkedIn, Munjal said that he will now transition to the role of executive chairman at the startup. Unacademy cofounder also added that he will be “fully involved” in the day-to-day operations of the recently-acquired startup and will “help” with upGrad’s initial public offering (IPO). Meanwhile, Unacademy chief business officer (CBO) Akhilendra Kumar will take over as the chief executive of the recently-acquired edtech platform. “I'm moving from CEO to executive chairman of Unacademy, and Akhilendra Kumar will take over as CEO. To be clear, I'm not going anywhere. I'll stay fully involved in operations every day, work alongside Akhilendra and help with the upGrad IPO. Akhilendra is one of the sharpest operators I know, and I'm proud to have him lead us into this next chapter…,” Munjal said in the post. The reshuffle comes just two months after upGrad completed its acquisition of Unacademy for just over $200 Mn in September. (This story will be updated soon)

So, you think you’re an Elder Scrolls superfan? You say you’ve been there since The Elder Scrolls Arena on MS-DOS and have logged hundreds of hours in The Elder Scrolls Online? You say you’ve bought all of the roughly 5,000 re-releases and remasters of Skyrim that have been made available in the last 15 years?
Tell me, then: What do you think of The Elder Scrolls Travels: Shadowkey?
What’s that? You’ve never played Shadowkey? You weren’t there day one back in 2004, Nokia N-Gage in hand, ready to experience the game’s 176 x 208 resolution mobile hack-and-slash RPG combat for yourself? And you call yourself a real Elder Scrolls fan?
Well, don’t worry. Now you can fill in this crucial gap in your history without even having to track down functional, decades-old N-Gage hardware. That’s thanks to Shadowkey: Reforged, a free fan-made PC port that pairs updated art with the original game files and scripts for an upscaled, 4K experience that runs natively on PC, no N-Gage or emulator needed.
A few decades of upgrades
Moving from a pre-iPhone mobile game to a modern PC obviously comes with major graphical upgrades, powered by a completely rewritten PC graphics engine. What was once a cramped portrait orientation on the N-Gage has now been expanded for a 16:9 monitor standard that displays at up to 120 fps (though the game’s logic still matches the original game’s 25 fps). In addition to newly retextured character and environmental models, the new port also sports small touches like bloom lighting, rippling water, and an upgraded interface with sharper text rendering than was possible on an ancient mobile phone.

IAEA increasingly concerned about Iranian enrichment plant, its report says
Iran has not permitted International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) officers to inspect the plant or see design plans, according to a confidential report released on Friday (Nov 13) that was seen by Reuters.
VIENNA: The UN nuclear watchdog is "increasingly concerned" about a uranium-enrichment plant at Isfahan that Iran declared to it last year but has still not let the watchdog inspect, it said in a confidential report on Iran on Friday (Nov 13) seen by Reuters.
Iran has not let International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) inspectors return to any of its nuclear facilities bombed by Israel and the United States in a 12-day campaign in June last year that destroyed or badly damaged Iran's other uranium enrichment plants, the heart of its nuclear programme.
The targets included a tunnel network at Isfahan where diplomats have said they believe the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP) - declared to the agency on Jun 12, 2025 - is located, though a senior diplomat said that its whereabouts and status remained unknown.
The IAEA had planned to inspect the plant on Jun 13, 2025 but the bombing campaign started that day, making it impossible.
"The Agency does not know IFEP's exact location, status for safeguards purposes or whether it contains nuclear material," the confidential IAEA report to member states said, adding that "the Agency is also increasingly concerned that Iran has not permitted the Agency" to inspect the plant or see design plans.
IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said in March his agency believed a significant amount of Iran's most highly enriched uranium was in the tunnel complex at Isfahan.
While the report singled out IFEP, it also reiterated that Iran should inform the IAEA of the status of its enrichment plants as well as its stock of highly enriched uranium, which includes material close to weapons grade, and let inspectors return to the bombed sites and account for the enriched uranium.
"The Agency's lack of information about this nuclear material and access to facilities to verify it is a matter of serious proliferation concern .... and needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency," it said.

Quick Answer
Nothing OS 5 brings a bunch of useful upgrades, from on-phone widget creation and new lockscreen clocks to split Quick Settings, Dual-View Video, easier iPhone sharing, the Glyph app, translucent themes, smarter QR scanning, and the new Geist font.
Nothing has updated all of its eligible devices to the latest version of its operating system, Nothing OS 5. It runs on top of Android 17, and in typical Nothing tradition, is clean and uncluttered. And while it might seem broadly similar to its predecessor, there are a number of interesting new features – some important, some seemingly trivial – beneath that familiar surface. So if you have a Nothing phone and it has received the Nothing OS 5 update (there is a list of supported devices with rollout timelines here: https://in.nothing.tech/nothing-os), here are eleven things you must try out.
Table of Contents
Appy fizz: Now build snazzy widgets right on your phone, no coding experience required
One of the biggest innovations of the Nothing ecosystem was the introduction of Essential apps that let users, even with no coding knowledge, make widgets. In the past, you had to access Essential Apps on a computer to be able to make these widgets. Now you can do so right on your phone. And it is as easy as easy peasy apple squeezie. Mind you, you still need to sign up for Essential Apps and be part of a waiting list before you can get into design mode. No download is needed – the Essential Apps app comes to your Nothing phone when you update the phone to Nothing OS 5.g
Get a gooey or an info-loaded lockscreen clock!
On to the really serious stuff now. Perhaps the most noticeable visual change in NothingOS is the addition of two lockscreen clock widgets – Gooey and Micrographics. The Gooey clock has a bold and fluid look, with numbers looking a little melted. It is very eye-catching and, well, different. Those who want a truckload of information on their lockscreen and who opt for Micrographics get details like day, date, weather, temperature, upcoming appointments, and, of course, the time, all in rows that give it a very business ticker feel. This is how you clock into this feature:
- Long-press on the lock screen of your phone. This will show a Customize lock screen text bubble. Tap on it, and then tap on the fingerprint scanner to get into the Lock screen edit zone.
- Tap the clock widget space, which shows the time, and you will see Clock face options.
- Gooey is the second option, and right next to it is Micrographics. Choose the one you want, and also tweak its color as per your wish.
- Tap on Done, and hey, it’s, well…done.
Our own preference is the Micrographics widget, which is incredibly handy. We hope they add email and other notifications to it as well.
Split those notifications and quick settings
In the past – as on many phones – swiping down on a Nothing phone showed one new notifications, and swiping further down gave one access to Quick Settings (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Brightness, Torch, et al.). Well, you can split them into two separate zones if you wish. Once done, swiping from one side of the top will give you access to Quick Settings, while swiping from the other will show notifications. To do this segregation, just follow these steps:
- Open Settings and go to Notifications
- Go to the Notifications and Quick Settings Option
- You will see two options: Separate and Combined (classic).
- Select Separate, and now Notifications and Quick Settings will occupy different parts of the top panel.
Find out how long you have been away from your phone
One of the coolest new widgets on Nothing OS 5 is the Away Time widget, which lets you know how long you have kept away from your phone, and shows it in a simple, clean widget that can be placed on your home screen or your lock screen. It is a nice way to know about the “me time” you have given yourself away from your phone. Getting it is as easy as pressing on any place on the lock screen or Home Screen, and then selecting the Away Time widget option. We suggest going for the larger (4 x 2) one because it just looks so much better, especially with that zen-like blue background.
Keep what matters on the Home Screen – use Collector
Another widget (yes, Nothing seems to really like them widgets) that is very handy is Collector. You just open it and place images of what you want to keep seeing or consider important in it, and it automatically cuts out what it sees as important and keeps it handy on the home screen. It has a wonderful fridge sticker vibe, and keeps what matters close at hand. Just long-press on the home screen and select it from the widget collection!
Glyph Interface? There’s an app for that – finally!
The Glyph Interface has been one of the most eye-catching features of Nothing’s phones. This is basically a collection of LEDs on the back of the phones that light up in different patterns, showing notifications and battery levels, letting you know who is calling, controlling volume, setting timers, and doing more, all on the back of the phone. There was a catch, though. The Glyph UI had to be controlled from the settings of the phone, which seemed to be a rather roundabout way of doing things. This has now been fixed with the Glyph app, which gives one direct access to the Glyph Interface, letting one tweak it without having to get into the Settings. No downloads needed – the Glyph app appears on your Nothing phone the moment you update it to Nothing OS 5.
Lights, camera action…with both front and back cameras
Nothing OS 5 gives you the option to shoot videos using the rear as well as the front camera simultaneously. One can choose from having the footage one below the other, or having the selfie camera in an inset and the main camera in the larger part of the display. To access the option:
- Launch the Camera app
- Scroll across to More and choose Dual-View Video
It would have been nice to be able to take some stills with this feature, but as of now, it is limited to video.
There’s a glassy, classy “translucent” theme
Yep, your Nothing phone is now on the glass UI bandwagon. Mind you, this option is not turned on by default. You will need to follow these steps:
- Go to Settings, and then choose Customization
- Choose Theme & Style, and then choose Translucent. You can opt to have a dark theme in this if you wish.
- Honestly, it is not exactly eye-popping as of now. The translucence seems mainly to be around the widgets, and the app icons are not translucent. But it is a good starting point.
Scan that QR code, even if it wobbles
This is a pretty minor and yet handy change in Nothing OS 5. While camera icons have all been polished, a tiny yet useful tweak is in scanning QR codes, especially when using the scanner in crowded places or in slightly wobbly situations (think of paying in a moving vehicle). Now, when you use the camera to scan a QR code, the link it leads to remains on the screen, even if your hand moves and the QR code goes off or the code itself wobbles a little. So scanning codes is a whole lot easier, and you don’t have to bother about lining up the camera with the QR code all the time.
Send images to THAT friend with the iPhone easily (no app needed)
With Nothing OS 5, sending images to iPhones is pretty easy. Here’s how you do it:
- Ask your friend to switch on AirDrop on their iPhone and allow everyone to send images to it.
- Select the images you want to send on your Nothing phone.
- Select the Quick Share option, and then select the Use QR Code option.
- Scan the QR code with the iPhone’s camera. The images will be transferred.
Get the new font, Geist

Oranges investigated after four girls die in suspected Uganda school poisoning
- Published
Ugandan police are investigating the deaths of four pupils at a school in the capital Kampala which they suspect may be the result of poisoning.
The four girls, aged between nine and 11 years, died on Tuesday. Three of the pupils died at home while the fourth passed away while receiving emergency treatment at a hospital.
The head teacher at the school, Ta'aliim Primary School and Quran Memorisation Centre, has been arrested to assist with investigations.
According to the school, eight pupils had eaten oranges shared by a fellow pupil.
Five pupils, including the four who later died, started vomiting. The fifth is still in hospital.
Post-mortem examinations are being carried out to determine the exact cause of death.
A police spokesperson was quoted by local media as saying that detectives would visit the village where the oranges the pupils ate came from.
The centre has been cordoned off as a crime scene.
Ugandan media shared videos of grieving parents describing their children's final moments, with some accusing the school of failing to provide clear and timely information.
The police have offered condolences to the bereaved families and affected community and say more information will be provided in due course.
The tragedy comes at a time when concerns are mounting over health and safety conditions in schools across Uganda.
Previous cases involving suspected contaminated food and exposure to harmful substances have left pupils hospitalised with symptoms including stomach pain, vomiting and breathing difficulties.
The incidents have intensified calls for authorities to strengthen monitoring of school feeding schemes, improve hygiene standards and ensure safer learning environments for children.

Chhath Puja is being celebrated with regional fervour. The festival is marked by Nahay Khaye. It is the first day of the four-day Hindu festival Chhath Puja, which symbolises physical and spiritual purification before beginning the sacred fast. The celebrations reach their peak during Sandhya Arghya, when devotees offer prayers to the setting Sun, which is observed after Usha Arghya to the rising Sun the next morning. If you are planning to witness the vibrant celebrations of Surya Shashti, several destinations across India offer a glimpse into the festival's traditions, devotion and cultural significance.
Yamuna Ghat
Yamuna Ghat is one of the most popular ghats located in Delhi and is among the places associated with Chhath Puja celebrations. Devotees gather along the Yamuna riverbanks and designated ghats to offer Arghya to the Sun God. The area comes alive with traditional songs, decorated offerings and festive gatherings.
Devotees prepare traditional offerings, including thekua, fruits and sugarcane, before offering prayers while standing in the water. The spiritual atmosphere makes it a significant spot to witness the festival.
Patna Ghats
Patna is among the most prominent destinations for experiencing Chhath Puja. Ghats along the Ganga, including Gandhi Ghat and Digha Ghat, attract thousands of devotees. The riverbanks are decorated with lights, flowers and traditional arrangements.
Varanasi
The famous ghats of Varanasi, including Dashashwamedh and Assi, witness special Chhath Puja prayers. Devotees gather along the Ganga to offer Arghya and perform rituals of Chhati Maiya on the ghats.
Howrah Bridge ghat in West Bengal
In West Bengal, Howrah Bridge ghat is the most famous for Chhath Puja celebrations. Rabindra Sarobar and Subhas Sarobar are other prominent places to offer Arghya to the Sun and perform Chhath Puja rituals.
Ranchi's water bodies
Ranchi also celebrates Chhath Puja with great enthusiasm. Devotees gather at popular water bodies, including Hatia Dam and other designated ponds, to perform the traditional rituals.
Whether in Delhi, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh or Jharkhand, Chhath Puja is a time to experience India's rich cultural traditions and deep-rooted devotion to nature.

Sandpapergate: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins dismisses Usman Khawaja's claims over ball-tampering scandal as 'utter nonsense'
Usman Khawaja said in new book 'Sabr' that every Australia player was aware of ball-tampering scheme in Cape Town in 2018; current Test captain Pat Cummins, who played in the match, reiterated his denial of involvement and dismissed Khawaja's claims as "utter nonsense"
Friday 13 November 2026 00:11, UK
Australia Test captain Pat Cummins dismissed his former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims as "utter nonsense" after the recently retired batter said in his autobiography that the whole side were aware of ball-tampering that took place on their 2018 tour of South Africa.
Khawaja made the revelations in his new book 'Sabr', which was released earlier this week, bringing the scandal back onto the agenda eight years after Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper on the ball while Australia were fielding.
Only Bancroft, then-captain Steve Smith and his vice-captain David Warner were punished, with each receiving lengthy bans as the rest of the Australian team and coaching staff denied knowledge of the scheme.
Cummins, who was a relatively junior member of the side playing in just his 13th Test match, in 2021 issued a joint-statement with fellow bowlers from the fixture Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, in which they denied knowing that a foreign substance had been taken onto the field to alter the ball in order to try to make it swing.
"When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he's 100 per cent wrong. I've said that consistently for the last eight years," Cummins told reporters on Friday morning in Sydney having called the press conference himself on social media.
"I did not know that was happening, but Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that.
"He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense."
Following the publication of the book, Warner, who received a year-long ban from all cricket and a lifetime ban from leadership roles, said on Monday that Khawaja's version of events was "100 per cent accurate".
Cummins, who was appointed Australia captain in November 2021, criticised Khawaja for being "casual" with the lives of his former team-mates and Australian cricket as a whole.
"Usman's a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations," Cummins said.
"In his book, Ussie has been casual with my life and the lives of many others, and I think Australian cricket."
Cummins, who appeared to become emotional at times in a press conference that lasted more than an hour, revealed that a video taken of him and his wife Becky in a heated discussion a day earlier had been prompted by her anger with Khawaja's actions.
Despite that and his clear disagreement with Khawaja's statements, Cummins said that he does not intend to pursue legal action.
"I did get advised this week that some of the things that've been said are probably defamatory, but I won't be doing that," Cummins said.
"You've got to move on. It's been eight years. We're moving on. So you got to draw a line at some point."
Cummins has been rested for England's white-ball tour of Australia, which resulted in him holding his press conference on Friday morning in Sydney just hours before the first ODI was scheduled to begin in Perth.
How have other Australian players reacted?
Cummins' extraordinary press conference came a day after Australia ODI captain Mitchell Marsh, who was also part of the team that toured South Africa in 2018, declined to comment on a series of questions about Khawaja's book.
Khawaja also claimed in the book that Australia experimented with lifting the seam on the ball during the 2017-18 Ashes at home to England, which they won 4-0 under the captaincy of Smith.
Starc, who had spoken to reporters on Tuesday, took a similar line to Cummins as he insisted that his recollections hadn't changed.
Starc, who is also not part of Australia's limited-overs side to face England, said of Khawaja's claims: "I haven't really paid much attention to it to be fair.
"There are differing opinions of eight years ago. We were heavily grilled through the process, at the time and since.
"I won't speak on behalf of the bowlers but from where I stand my opinion hasn't changed, my recollection hasn't changed from what we said in 2021.
"As far as our statement said, we weren't aware of things being taken on the field. That's where I'll leave it.
"I will be sticking to what I said five years ago, what I said at the time eight years ago, so clearly there are differing versions from different people.
"We weren't aware of anything taken on the field to be tampered with. We saw it on the big screen in Cape Town.
"As far as the book is concerned, I haven't read it. I probably won't read it, so that's for Usman to elaborate on."

Ukraine says it has captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war, amid what it says is a spike in recruitment by Russia from the south-east Asian nation.
The 49-year-old man from Java was taken to Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region to take part in a Russian assault, but managed to reach Ukrainian-held territory after the group came under drone attack, according to Ukraine’s state-run I Want to Live project. He was then captured by the Ukrainians.
According to the project, some 283 Indonesians were recruited in the first nine months of this year to fight for Russia against Ukraine. It said recruitment from Indonesia was no more than 10 in the previous three years.
The Russian embassy in Jakarta did not immediately respond to questions about the alleged recruitment effort but it is not the first time Russia has sought foreign mercenaries for its war effort.
In February, Kenya’s intelligence services reported that more than 1,000 Kenyans had been lured to fight for Russia.
A growing number of people from African countries – including Kenya, Uganda and South Africa – and elsewhere have been lured to the frontline as Russia seeks help to sustain its more than four-year war after invading Ukraine in February 2022.
This month Jakarta urged Moscow to ensure no Indonesians were drafted into its military, following the reported death in October of an Indonesian national serving with the military.
Indonesian foreign ministry spokesperson Yvonne Mewengkang said: “The Indonesian government asked the Russian government to take all necessary steps to ensure that no Indonesians will be recruited into the Russian military or any other military-related position in Russia through any avenues.”
Indonesia, she added, was particularly concerned about recruitment practices that could constitute human trafficking.
Days later, Indonesian police said they had identified a human trafficking syndicate targeting its nationals that used social media and messaging apps to recruit victims.
The posts promised lucrative jobs in logistics, border security and defence construction, but after the applicants travelled to Russia they were directed to sign contracts to serve as mercenaries, with some deployed to conflict zones, police said.
The ‘I Want to Live’ governmental initiative was established in September 2022 by the coordination headquarters for Prisoners of War with support from Ukraine defence ministry and defence intelligence (HUR).
It was designed to allow active-duty troops, including Russian servicemen and foreign nationals recruited into the Russian military, to safely surrender and exit the battlefield.

Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?
- Published
After a shock announcement 10 months ago that the Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) would be held every four years, the governing body of football on the continent has reversed course.
The Confederation of African Football (Caf) will instead retain the tournament's traditional biennial staging, with its president Patrice Motsepe saying the U-turn was based on "advancing, protecting and promoting" the interests of the African game.
The first indication that the frequency of Afcon was being reconsidered came at Caf's strategy conference in Cape Verde earlier this month.
Questions are now being asked about the decision-making process and what this means for the future of African football.
Why was the planned change controversial?
Afcon has predominantly been held every two years since its first edition in 1957, barring two three-year gaps in the 1960s and one year between the 2012 and 2013 tournaments.
On the eve of the 2025 finals in Morocco, Motsepe announced all that would change from 2028.
The South African said the shift to a four-year cycle was, in part, to help the global calendar "be significantly more synchronised and harmonised".
In recent years Afcon has been staged midway through the European club season, leading to recurring disputes over the release of African players.
Fifa general secretary Mattias Grafstrom was sitting aside Motsepe when the plan was announced, and critics highlighted that the scheduling change favoured football's world governing body more than the African game.
"I think the general sentiment around the continent has been that the two-year cycle has served the continent very well," Football Association of Zambia (Faz) official Sydney Mungala told the BBC.
"The idea of pushing it to a four-year cycle was a bit of a surprise, maybe a concern, to the bulk of the African federations."
- Afcon to return to two-year cycle after Caf U-turn 
  - Published21 hours ago
- Afcon to be held every four years from 2028 
  - Published20 December 2025
What were the benefits of the switch?
Afcon has developed into Caf's biggest revenue generator, with a profit of $114m (£85m) forecast for Afcon 2025, up from $75m (£56m) for the previous finals in Ivory Coast.
In its stead, an annual Africa Nations League involving all 54 countries on the continent was proposed. Motsepe described the ambition as creating a "world-class competition every year".
The idea was to move beyond Caf's heavy reliance on Afcon and develop a more sustainable commercial model which could support football development.
Yet the last time an ambitious alternative competition took place in Africa, it failed to deliver on its financial promise and was quickly ditched.
The Africa Super League, announced by Caf in 2022 to revolutionise continental club competition, and with projected annual revenues of $200m (£149m), was discontinued after just one edition.
Motsepe later acknowledged that commercial deals fell short of expectations.
"We didn't proceed as quickly because the partners that were giving us money were not giving us the deals we thought we would be happy with," he said.
Why the U-turn on Afcon?
The decision to move to a four-year cycle was taken at a meeting of Caf's executive committee last December - without being tabled at a general assembly where all member nations are represented.
"These kinds of decisions should be put to the general assembly, they should be debated and discussed for months at a time," Algerian journalist Maher Mezahi told the BBC.
"Afcon is the locomotive by which Caf funds all of its other competitions."
Caf subsequently asked its 54 associations to express a preference between proceeding with the four-year format or retaining the original schedule, and the executive committee eventually voted to restore the status quo.
Motsepe said the decision was in the "best interest of African football" and would contribute to the development and growth of the sport.
He also admitted misgivings about the new Nations League, with concerns it would require "several years" before it could make "the substantial financial and football development contributions" to help the continental game be "self-supporting".
How does Fifa fit in?
Fifa president Gianni Infantino first publicly proposed holding Afcon every four years in February 2020, an idea Motsepe rejected after he was elected as Caf president 13 months later.
That has not stopped the South African cultivating a close relationship with his counterpart and Infantino's drive to expand the Fifa World Cup to 48 teams - and in the process increase African representation at the tournament - has won him backing across the continent.
Yet the Swiss' position has been under threat since his plan to sell stakes in Fifa's competitions was leaked in July.
Since then Infantino has been busy shoring up his power base ahead of his re-election bid, including at Caf's strategy meeting this month.
"He came to Cape Verde to generate support, And, by and large, Africa gave him that support," Mezahi said.
"But I think they did that in a quid pro quo - they gave him the support in return for some concessions.
"And I think the main concession was the return of the Africa Cup of Nations [to a two-year cycle].
"It shows that Africa is willing to assert its influence and look after its interests, even in the face of the global game's interest."
- Infantino says he is backed by 'vast majority' 
  - Published6 days ago
- Does Africa still back Infantino as Fifa president? 
  - Published6 August
Why is Afcon revenue so important?
Afcon is Caf's financial lifeline, accounting for a substantial share of the governing body's income.
Morocco 2025 was projected to generate $192m (£143m), representing 66% of Caf's total revenue from competitions across men's, women's and age-group football.
For many FAs, Afcon's importance extends far beyond the tournament because they cannot always rely on consistent government or corporate investment.
"We have 11 [Zambian] national teams and only two are partly sponsored by government," Faz official Mungala said.
"The rest have to be supported from the FA's coffers. We actually fund some of these programmes from the support that we get from Caf and Fifa."
What about upcoming Afcons?
The 2027 Afcon is scheduled to be held in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from 19 June to 17 July next year.
Yet, on a visit to East Africa in September, Motsepe called for a "heightened sense of urgency" in order to make sure stadiums and supporting infrastructure are ready on time.
The next Afcon will be held just one year later in 2028 - a decision Caf made when planning for the switch to a four-year cycle and which it as has decided to stick with.
An announcement on where and exactly when the finals will be held is yet to be made.
Subsequent tournaments will be held in 2031 and 2033 to avoid clashes with the World Cup.
The proposed kick-off date for the Africa Nations League, meanwhile, is September 2029.
Motsepe's latest statement suggests the new competition will also be held every two years - rather than annually as he initially announced last December – but that begs the question of how space will be found for the fixtures to be played in an Afcon year from 2031 onwards.
While debate continues around the game's congested calendar, Caf's U-turn on scheduling has at least protected the tradition of Africa's biggest sporting showcase.
It also exposes, however, the challenge of finding a workable financial model which benefits African football as well as the demands of the global game.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office has denied reports of a heated exchange with US President Donald Trump during a phone conversation over the weekend, which reportedly centred on the possibility of resuming military strikes against Iran.
According to a report by Hebrew-language outlet Ynet, cited by The Times of Israel, Netanyahu's office rejected the allegations, describing them as "Fake news, complete nonsense". The denial came after anonymous sources familiar with the conversation described it as particularly tense, with one source reportedly calling it a "shouting match from hell."
The Times of Israel also reported that a senior Israeli official confirmed the phone call had taken place. However, the official told Ynet that it was “very much not a difficult conversation.”
The denial comes amid reports that Netanyahu has repeatedly pressed Trump in recent days to launch another military offensive against Iran.
According to The Times of Israel, the Israeli Prime Minister has been urging Washington to consider renewed military action even as Trump weighs the possibility of pursuing a diplomatic solution against escalating military tensions.
Earlier in the week, Trump indicated that further military strikes against Iran were not immediately necessary.
However, The Times of Israel noted that Trump said on Thursday that the United States does not “need a deal with Tehran.”
Meanwhile, Defence Minister Israel Katz met today with IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir and other senior defence and security officials, asserting that all decisions made during the current transitional period of coalition talks are being handled "responsibly" and in complete coordination with the military.
The Times of Israel reported that Katz's office quoted him as saying, "Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, I and the IDF chief of staff see eye to eye on the Iranian issue in all its aspects, and we will continue to work together and do whatever is necessary to ensure the security of the State of Israel and protect its citizens."
The defence minister's office further noted that Katz emphasised during the assessment that "all decisions are made responsibly and in full cooperation between the political and military leadership," underscoring that "Israel’s security is the central consideration," according to The Times of Israel.
The Times of Israel added that these remarks come after Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot—who currently holds the mandate to form a new government—cautioned Netanyahu against deploying security forces in the absence of an immediate threat, following reports that the caretaker prime minister has been pushing for military strikes on Iran over the objections of defence officials.
Meanwhile, citing Hebrew media reports, Times of Israel reported thatPrime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has begun his security briefing with Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot.
The Prime Minister’s Office does not immediately confirm the reports.
This comes after Israeli media reported that Trump and Netanyahu engaged in a heated telephone conversation over the preceding days, which reportedly deteriorated into an acrimonious exchange amid ongoing disagreements regarding the course of the war with Iran.
According to reports from Israeli news organisations Ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth, the Israeli leader repeatedly pushed for renewed military action, whereas the American President preferred allowing ongoing peace negotiations with Tehran to continue.
Netanyahu has consistently argued that Washington should resume strikes and actively pursue regime change within the Islamic Republic, while Trump has favoured maintaining economic pressure to secure diplomatic concessions from Tehran. The Israeli Prime Minister's Office rejected claims that the conversation became confrontational, describing the reports as "fake news".
Israeli news outlets Ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth reported that Netanyahu repeatedly urged Trump to restart the war during the call. Trump, however, continued to back a diplomatic approach as talks with Iran progressed.
Sources quoted by both outlets described the conversation as having descended into a "shouting match from hell". A senior Israeli official confirmed that the two leaders spoke over the weekend but denied that any confrontation had taken place.
The latest reports emerged days after the Financial Times said Netanyahu had been telephoning Trump daily to persuade him to resume an all-out war. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, is facing uncertainty over his position after losing seats in the general election held in October.

In a major change to screening guidelines, the American Cancer Society recommended on Thursday that American men between ages 50 and 69 at an average risk of prostate cancer should test their prostate-specific antigen (PSA) blood levels every two years.
The prior guidelines, released in 2010, left testing for average-risk men to their discretion, after assessing cancer risk with a physician.
Similarly, PSA testing recommendations were strengthened for high risk groups — Black men and men with a strong family history of prostate cancer. They are now encouraged to get PSA-based screening yearly starting at 45. Black men in particular disproportionately die from prostate cancer, and the guideline authors said they hope that increased surveillance will reduce the number of Black patients presenting with cancers at advanced stages.
Then, starting at 70, the decision on whether to continue screening becomes individualized as the balance of benefit and harm is not as clear after that age. Screening should be interrupted after 80, or in men who are not expected to live another 10 years.
The changes reflect recent findings that screening through PSA levels reduced disease specific mortality for certain men, bringing the indicator back into specialists’ good graces. Once a preferred biomarker to identify risk of prostate cancer, routine PSA screening had fallen out of favor — and was dropped from the guidelines in 2010 — for its lack of specificity, which resulted in many men undergoing follow-up procedures when they had no cancer, or very slow-growing tumors.
The U.S. Preventive Service Task Force, a federally appointed panel of outside experts, has not changed its guidelines since the new evidence became available in 2025, and continues to recommend against routine, population-wide PSA screening, suggesting instead individualized decision-making. But the panel, whose recommendations determine the preventive services that insurers must cover, has announced an upcoming update.
The cutoff for PSA levels to be considered high is established as 3.0 nanograms/milliliter or higher for men aged 45 to 69 years old. This is an important clarification, said James Eastham, chief of urology at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. “Most PSA blood tests in the United States, when they’re reported, say under 4.0 [ng/ml] is normal, but it really should be under 3,” he said. “I think [the update] will hopefully help primary care physicians refer folks a little bit earlier.”
To limit the risk of overdiagnosis and overtreatment, the guidelines also now recommend two elevated PSA readings, followed by an MRI scan and/or testing for other biomarkers of prostate cancer, with the aim of reducing the number of patients undergoing biopsies. “We just wanted to give a little bit of flexibility for folks who cannot easily obtain an MRI,” said William Dahut, chief scientific officer at the ACS and a contributing author of the guidelines, about including both biomarkers and MRIs as a possible step following elevated PSA levels. However, he noted that an MRI would still be recommended prior to biopsy, should a biomarker test come back abnormal.
Though there are a variety of biomarkers, the guidelines don’t recommend one over the other. Dahut said ACS researchers intend to look more closely at biomarkers to establish which may be more effective in predicting a more aggressive cancer.
“I think the new guidelines are certainly a balanced approach for early detection of prostate cancer,” said Eastham. “There have been many men undergoing unnecessary biopsies, and many low risk cancers that were subsequently overtreated,” he said. By recommending some steps between an elevated PSA and a biopsy, he said, the new recommendations reflect the evidence that while being a good biomarker, PSA alone would identify too many men as biopsy candidates.
Finally, the guidelines emphasize the importance of active surveillance in men with slow growing cancer: “If you screen more men, you’re going to find more men with early-stage disease, and we need to be strong in our position that that does not mean that you need to rush for therapies or that you need to have therapies at all.”
For Eddie Baynes, a 56-year-old prostate cancer survivor and advocate, the new guidelines “hit the nail on the head” when it comes to recommending routine PSA screening. As a Black man, he knew he was at higher risk of developing prostate cancer, yet it wasn’t until the fraternity he belonged to organized a screening event that he, at 52, started getting regular PSA tests with his bloodwork. Though routine screening wasn’t part of the ACS recommendation at the time, it led to a cancer diagnosis and a prostatectomy.
That’s why he’s been advocating for men to get PSA levels tested, and relatively frequently. With the new guidelines, men like him will start routine screening earlier than he did. “Part of my advocacy is getting tested more frequently. So now, just to have that announcement coming from the American Cancer Society, it just makes what I’ve been urging individuals to do for a while stronger,” he said.

ByteDance is reportedly working on its own AI agent
The Chinese company wants to compete with Meta’s Muse.
ByteDance wants to take on Meta's Muse with its own AI agent. The company is readying an AI assistant that could be revealed in "the coming weeks," Bloomberg reports.
The report doesn't detail what the agent will be called or how it will work, but says that it will "serve a similar role" to Meta's Muse. Muse has already drawn more than 10 million users and CEO Mark Zuckerberg has predicted the AI agent could generate more revenue per user than its existing "family" of apps. The agent is also expected to play a significant role in Meta's AI glasses, and the company has previewed a standalone "charm" for Muse.
It's not clear if ByteDance is also planning on incorporating its agent into hardware. The AI assistant is one piece of the Chinese company's strategy to compete with frontier AI companies. ByteDance cofounder Zhang Yiming recently told employees that it would likely take "until at least 2029 or 2030" for the company's AI efforts to catch up, Bloomberg reported. Within the AI space, ByteDance has been primarily known for its video generator, Seedance. Clips from the video model went viral on social media platforms earlier this year, which eventually drew legal scrutiny from US-based studios.
If the TikTok maker does introduce its own AI agent, it would also likely raise new concerns about data privacy and how much access personal agents should get. ByteDance didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
