Get in, loser: Broadway's newest 'Mean Girls' are ready to insult (and enlighten) you
What would it mean to become Miss Ghana 1986? Fame, fortune, perhaps rubbing elbows with '80s superstar Bobby Brown? For a group of six teenage girls at the Aburi Girls Boarding School, the answer is: everything.
The battle for the crown is at the heart of School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play, written by Tony Award-nominated playwright Jocelyn Bioh. The play is ending a Broadway run this week and celebrating with livestream broadcasts on The League of Live Stream Theater's website for a fee (but is free for high schoolers).
School Girls is set at a boarding school in Ghana in 1986. It follows Paulina, the school's queen bee and her crew, whom she frequently belittles and bullies over their looks.
"So, do you want to be fat-fat? Or fit? And popular." Paulina asks Nana, harassing her over eating porridge instead of an apple at lunch.
Ahead of a visit from a pageant recruiter to the school, Paulina's plans to win Miss Ghana go awry after a new transfer student arrives: Ericka from … Ohio!
Ericka exposes Paulina's toxic behavior and shows her up during a performance of Whitney Houston's Greatest Love of All. Ericka, being lighter-skinned than Paulina, sparks a clash between the school's headmistress and the pageant director over beauty and who would have the best chance of winning the Miss Global Universe pageant.
Paulina becomes the victim of circumstances that she cannot control.
School Girls explores the themes of girlhood and impossible societal beauty standards with humor and humanity.
Although its title references the Tina Fey-penned 2004 film, Mean Girls, famous for its pink-hued portrayal of the toxic side of high school girls, Bioh says she wasn't actively thinking about the movie when writing School Girls.
After completing the play and needing to settle on a subtitle, Bioh found herself reflecting on the themes: "I'm like we're dealing with things and ideas and feelings and emotions." She said that her friend, actress Danai Gurira, described it as feral teenage girls. "I'm like, that archetype is incredibly universal."
A perspective on colorism
Beyond the talk about tiaras, '80s fashion and praise for Judy Bloom, School Girls tackles the issue of colorism head-on.
Bioh says she knew it was a topic she always wanted to write about after her own long journey to own her beauty as a dark-skinned woman. "I just wanted to write something that felt like it could maybe shorten the journey for somebody else who maybe felt the same way I did. Especially as a young, impressionable girl."
While School Girls approaches the topic from the perspective of Ghanaian women and girls, Bioh says the play's message has resonated with people from different backgrounds, underscoring that colorism is a global issue.
"'Cause who has decided that this one standard of beauty is the standard of beauty for everybody? I think that's a problem," Bioh explains. "I don't have a solution other than to, you know, create a play that people can feel entertained by or perhaps be impacted by, and hopefully shift their implicit bias as they move through the world."
The cast of School Girls displays a vast array of talent: Denée Benton (Paulina), Lucia Aremu (Ama), Nia Otchere-Sarfo (Gifty), Jordan Rice (Mercy), Erin Morton (Nana) and Jasmine Amy Rogers (Ericka), just to name a few. While it is an all-Black female cast, the diversity of physical appearance is clear.
"The audience, even if they are not young Black girls who went to school in Ghana, they still see facets of themselves in these girls. I think that's where the heart and beauty of it lies." Bioh says.
Audience reaction
School Girls is now on Broadway nearly 10 years after its Off-Broadway premiere. She says it's been a moving experience to see how the show's message continues to stay with audiences long after they leave the theater.
"I had a DM from Jenna Fischer of all people, who went to see the play a few days ago, and literally messaged me again today to say she's still thinking about the play," she says. "You know, how cool that someone who I just absolutely adore and also think is, like, a comedic genius, but who likely has never had any sort of experience with colorism, is still thinking about what the play is saying and how much it moved her.
For those who get to experience School Girls, Bioh hopes you have a good time and walk away with a deep sense of empathy not only for the young girls but for the adult women too.
"I ask people to shift their ideas about things," Bioh says. "If you can just move it just a little teeny bit, then I guess, you know, I've done my job."

The first big sex scandal of the AI era has taken down Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder and longtime CEO. Nvidia’s board of directors announced his resignation on Thursday morning and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.
Jensen Huang is out. What now?
The former Nvidia CEO’s downfall is far bigger than one company.
Huang has been making headlines all week after news broke Friday that he had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singaporean tech firm Megaspeed who the US government alleges was also a Chinese spy.
The revelation Wednesday of a second extramarital affair, this time with an Nvidia employee reporting to Huang directly, added to the pressure, and another affair came to light later on Thursday after Huang’s ouster.
The scandal has implications far beyond one company: Huang’s central role in the AI race can’t be overstated. It was his vision of an AI future that led him to pivot Nvidia from a small company making video game chips into the dominant player in making the chips that serve OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google’s computing needs.
Huang is close friends with President Donald Trump’s and a leading voice in resisting efforts to slow AI progress. And he has pushed for the US to take a less hawkish position toward China’s own AI goals, a stance now called into question by his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Among its other impacts, the news has revived efforts on Capitol Hill to further restrict chip exports to China.
To break down the national security implications of Huang’s departure, how the Trump administration is involved, and what it says about US AI industry writ large, Today, Explained co-host Sean Rameswaram spoke with Garret De Vynck, a technology reporter at the Washington Post.
Below is an excerpt of their conversation, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full podcast, so listen to Today, Explained wherever you get your podcasts, including Apple Podcasts, Pandora, and Spotify.
Nvidia has been called the central bank of AI, which is why it’s so important that we figure out what Jensen Huang may have disclosed to this alleged spy. How long has the president known about this, as far as we know?
As far as we know, the president has known about the fact that Jensen Huang was in a relationship with someone that the US government thought was a spy for about a year. This circulated within the administration, and the decision was made not to tell Jensen.
That doesn’t necessarily mean that it was automatically some kind of corrupt decision of President Trump protecting Jensen Huang. There’s all sorts of reasons why you might not want to tell someone they’re being spied on, the number one being that they might blow up the operation. Maybe you want to learn more. Maybe you suspect that the person themselves knows that they’re being spied on and is willingly sharing information and you need some more time to gather that. It’s unclear why the US government specifically chose not to pull in Jensen Huang.
It’s also a little bit unclear whether he knows he was being spied on, or whether maybe he was told through some kind of back channel. He has said that he did not know that she was a spy and he is admitting to the affair, to the infidelity. He’s admitting to essentially breaking Nvidia’s code of conduct by sleeping with one of its customers, but he is not admitting at all to knowing that she was a spy and definitely not admitting to sharing any information willfully.
It feels like this is the kind of thing that the government would investigate. There’s been reporting that the Commerce Department was involved with some kind of investigation, but that investigation came to an end and no one really knows why.
The context here is that the United States and China are in an AI race. Going back to the first Trump administration, there’s been pretty aggressive export controls saying, “We don’t want China to get our tech so that they can develop AI.” And the Biden administration continued that. He increased the export controls on China. China was complaining very loudly about this. They said, ‘We don’t care. We want to win AI and we need to slow you guys down.’
When Trump came in, he actually lifted his foot off the gas a little bit. They didn’t throw the gates open and say, “You can have whatever you want. All American companies can sell whatever they want to China.” But he said, “Some AI chips that are less powerful than the state of the art. We can send those to Chinese companies.“
The other thing that national security experts have pointed out is that the Trump administration could theoretically have been doing more to stop the smuggling of computer chips to China. And that’s where this story gets so important for national security.
Megaspeed is accused of essentially being a front for Chinese companies to get access to computer chips. Journalists have gone to Megaspeed’s office in Singapore where it’s based, and there were only a couple of people working there. It didn’t really seem like there was a lot going on. Nvidia has said all through this process over the last couple of years that, “No, we’ve checked it out, Megaspeed is a legitimate company and we’re not breaking the law when it comes to this.”
There are a lot of questions and what everyone is focused on finding out, both journalists and I would say congressional Democrats when they come into office in the new year is, is there something more going on here? Is there something where the Chinese either convinced Jensen Huang to sell more chips to them or Jensen Huang himself, who has been advocating for selling more chips to China, essentially did this himself?
“I think there’s this real question of: Do we see a much stronger push to actually ramp up controls on China and how does Trump respond?”
He’s been pressuring the president, he’s been donating to him, he’s been glad-handing with the president and the president has been listening more to this corporate executive who is his friend and who donated him a bunch of money rather than listening to China hawks or national security experts who say we should be limiting what China is able to access.
That’s really where the locus of this investigation is going to be. It’s not so much that Jensen Huang had an affair. It’s more the fact that he himself is someone who has said we need to sell more computer chips to China and he was involved with an alleged Chinese spy, and he’s very close to the president and had influence on the president.
You mentioned the Democrats. Have they said anything? Are they going to call him in front of Congress for an investigation?
Going forward, there are two big things here. One of them is these investigations into Jensen Huang and this whole situation. The company is likely going to continue to investigate. Maybe more information will come out there. Jensen Huang has been called to speak later this month in Congress. And congressional Democrats have also said that when they come into power in January, they will be asking him.
The second big thing that comes out of this is, what does America do when it comes to China and AI? Now that one of the biggest advocates for being a bit more friendly towards China when it comes to selling them things that they need for AI is out of the room and completely discredited, I think that the China hawks, those who say we need to crack down more aggressively, we need to limit China’s access to AI computer chips, they’re really coming into ascendance here and they’re in the Republican Party, they’re in the Democratic Party, some of them, people like Marco Rubio, are even in the Cabinet.
I think there’s this real question of: Do we see a much stronger push to actually ramp up controls on China and how does Trump respond? There’s all sorts of geopolitical things that could sort of spin out of this CEO affair.
I’m old enough to remember when a board tried to get rid of Sam Altman and then he was just back a week later. Elon Musk is already offering Jensen Huang a job. Is there a fair chance that he just goes somewhere that’s not that concerned about espionage affairs or getting with your VP of health or whatever it is? Is he just going to go work for China?
I don’t think he’s going to go work for China. This is definitely the wildest corporate story since Sam Altman was fired as CEO and brought back three or four days later. It’s a very different situation. That was a startup where you essentially have five or six investors who get to make the call about who the CEO is, and the employees at that company overwhelmingly wanted to bring Sam Altman back. I think they wanted more continuity of the company, but they also wanted to make sure that their company didn’t go under and go bankrupt and get disappeared, which was sort of on the table at that point in time.
Nvidia’s not going anywhere. Obviously employees have lost a lot of money in terms of the stock value already coming down due to the situation. So employees are probably shocked. They’re probably upset. Jensen Huang is broadly loved at Nvidia, and so I can definitely see that employees would be doing petitions, asking for him to return.
But this is a giant public company and the board makes a decision here. Jensen Huang was untruthful publicly and I think that also will make other public companies hesitant before rushing to bring him on as CEO.
As we’ve talked about many times in the show, half of our economy is staked on AI at this point. How concerned should we be that one of the most important people in this industry was so easily duped in this honeypot situation? Are these the people we should be trusting with the future of our society?
It’s a really good reminder that people are people. I think that we like to lionize individuals and say that they are the ones who are going to take us into the future and they are inventing the future and it’s so incredible. And I do think Jensen Huang gets a lot of credit for making sure that the companies kept up in AI, but at the end of the day, it was also a lucky break for them that the computer chips they were making just happened to work well for the math that is required by artificial intelligence.
I do think that this speaks to something that a lot of people across the country and maybe even the world really feel. They do not want to sign off the future to a dozen dudes in Silicon Valley and their collaborators in the Trump White House. I think that is a view that a lot of people increasingly have. I think it was one of the factors in the midterms, maybe not the most important one, but people are concerned about concentration of power. They’re concerned about AI and they don’t see it as something that they themselves have control over.
I think that this is just going to be another thing that sort of adds skepticism to the idea that people like Jensen Huang should be the ones making the final decision when it comes to artificial intelligence.

In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that all men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test.
Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday.
Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years.
Men ages 70 to 74 should consult their doctor on continuing screening, while those 75 and up are not recommended to get screened.
The new guidance departs from ACS’s previous iteration, published in 2010, which made no universal recommendations for routine screening. Men at age 50 were recommended to use shared-decision making with their doctors on whether or not to get tested. The recommendation was similar to that from the US Preventive Services Task Force, a federal panel that regularly evaluates evidence and makes recommendations on such preventive medical care. (The USPSTF is currently working on an update to its prostate cancer screening recommendation, though it should be noted that the panel has recently been overhauled by anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and new members are reportedly rife with conflicts of interest.)

The last few weeks have been turbulent for Nvidia, the world's largest semiconductor company by market capitalisation, and its CEO, Jensen Huang. The controversy began after reports revealed his alleged association with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US officials of having links to Chinese intelligence. Jensen Huang subsequently acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, although he did not identify the person involved. Allegations about Alice Huang's links to Chinese intelligence have yet to be independently established. Another report subsequently surfaced claiming that the Nvidia chief had been involved in a second extramarital affair. On Thursday (local time), Huang stepped down as the company's CEO. The developments come at a crucial time, with the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting scheduled to take place in Shenzhen on November 18–19. US President Donald Trump is expected to meet his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, on the sidelines of the summit, raising questions about whether the controversy surrounding Huang could cast a shadow over the high-stakes engagement. Several reports claimed that Trump had been informed about Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang. However, the US President has denied having prior knowledge of the matter, while also expressing sympathy for the Nvidia chief, who has grown increasingly close to him. Quick answers to key questions Huang resigned amid reports of extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, who has been suspected by US officials of links to Chinese intelligence. A report said Nvidia’s board acted after a second alleged affair surfaced. No. The Justice Department said it had not concluded whether Alice Huang was a spy, and the FBI was investigating reports of her alleged links to the Chinese government. The allegations have not been independently established. It could add complexity to the meeting because it comes amid tensions over semiconductor exports, AI and technology competition. Analysts cited in the article said the controversy was unlikely to immediately change Trump’s approach to Beijing. Nvidia’s advanced AI chips are central to the global race to develop powerful AI systems, making access to them a major issue for Washington and Beijing. Huang had urged the US to ease restrictions on chip sales to China. The article does not say that tighter controls are certain. It says the controversy has increased pressure from lawmakers in both parties to scrutinise Nvidia’s China sales and consider stricter limits on advanced AI chip exports. In an interview with Salem News Channel on Thursday (local time), Trump said, "Well, we gave it to Jensen, frankly, that was a little before — but what a horrible thing that is, that's so sad to see that happen." Bloomberg and The New York Times also reported that Trump had contacted Huang on separate occasions, urging him to remain in his position and checking on him following the controversy. With Huang's departure coming just days before the Trump-Xi meeting, a key question is whether the allegations involving the Nvidia chief could complicate the US President's engagement with Beijing, particularly amid tensions over semiconductor exports, artificial intelligence and technology competition. Nvidia and its former CEO, Jensen Huang, have become important figures in US-China technology relations. The company's advanced artificial intelligence chips are central to the global race to develop increasingly powerful AI systems, making access to its technology a major point of contention between Washington and Beijing. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, pushed Washington and Trump to ease restrictions on the sale of advanced AI chips to Beijing, arguing that wider access to the technology would help the country maintain its lead in AI development. In December 2025, the US President allowed sales of the H200, the chipmaker's second-most powerful AI chip, with roughly 25% of the proceeds going to the US government. Trump went ahead with the decision despite resistance from China hawks across both Republican and Democratic ranks. Huang was unexpectedly included in Trump's delegation to Beijing in May, as the administration sought to revive stalled sales of Nvidia's H200 chips. However, even after Trump approved the exports, shipments remained limited as Chinese authorities were slow to grant import clearances, reportedly to encourage the growth of domestic chip manufacturers. The latest controversy surrounding Huang could therefore complicate an already delicate US-China technology relationship, just days before Trump and Xi are expected to meet at the APEC summit. Trump is unlikely to immediately change his approach towards Beijing because of the controversy, according to analysts cited by Al Jazeera. Huang's departure from Nvidia is a "stalemate at best", Singapore-based geopolitical analyst Steve Okun told the publication, suggesting that the scandal is unlikely to significantly affect relations between Washington and Beijing. Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations, accusing Washington of using them as a pretext to restrict China's technological development. On Thursday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said, "The US side should stop fabricating such 'spy' narratives as a pretext for imposing a technological blockade." However, the controversy is increasing pressure on Trump and his administration at home, with lawmakers from both Republicans and Democrats calling for greater scrutiny of the company's dealings with China and the administration's handling of semiconductor exports. On Thursday, House Speaker Mike Johnson said there was a growing consensus in Congress on limiting semiconductor chip exports to China, adding that recent developments had strengthened the case for restrictions. Some lawmakers are also pushing for tighter controls on advanced AI chip sales to Beijing. This comes as US Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Department of Justice (DOJ) had yet to conclude whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy, while the FBI was investigating reports that she had worked for the Chinese government. Singapore has also clarified that its investigation involving Alice Huang was not related to espionage. The controversy may therefore not immediately change Trump's approach towards Beijing, but it could intensify domestic pressure for a tougher US technology policy. With Congress and hawkish voices within the administration calling for tighter export controls, the issue could add another layer of complexity to the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting. You can edit Instagram Reels on Mac using Claude AI and the free Instagram Edits app. Install Claude Code, enable the app’s MCP automation server, and connect both. Then use simple text prompts to create projects, arrange clips, add transitions, titles, and effects, and export finished Reels in 4K.
The wait is over. The Instagram Edits app is finally available on desktop, but only on macOS, as of this guide. Instagram Edits is my go-to app not just for editing Instagram Reels, but also a reliable free video editor with all the features and a simple design.
Although the app is designed for creators and competes with CapCut, it has been limited to Android and iOS so far. But a few months ago, Instagram announced a desktop version, and now it is finally here. Right now, the app is only available on macOS, with Windows and other platforms coming in future releases.
I have been using the app for the past couple of days. It is very similar to the mobile app and is also free to use, but it also features an MCP connection, which you can use to connect to any of your AI subscriptions, such as Claude, Codex, and Muse, and let AI edit your videos.
The desktop interface is slightly different and can be complex for beginners. It took me a while to get used to it, but I have created a detailed guide to get started.
I also created a guide on how to connect your MCP, like Claude, to Instagram Edits to edit your videos, and it covers everything about this feature, including common setup errors. This guide is for beginners, so each step is comprehensive and detailed.
Table of Contents
How to Connect Claude AI to Instagram Edits and Edit Reels on Mac
Before connecting your Instagram Edits app to the MCP server, ensure you have the following pre-requirements:
- A Mac with an Apple chip (M1 or newer) on macOS 15.1 or later. Currently, the Instagram Edits desktop app is only available for macOS, with Windows and Linux versions coming soon, but there is no expected release date yet.
- Download and install the Instagram Edits app from here
- A paid AI subscription for any model; you can also use the free AI model.
Part 1: Get Claude Code
Step 1: Open Terminal and type the command: claude –version, and press Return. If you see a version number, it means Claude Code is already installed on your device. You can skip to Part 2 to continue setup.
If you see something like zsh: command not found: claude, it means Claude Code is not installed on your device, or Terminal can not find it yet. Follow the next steps to install Claude Code on your Mac.
Install Claude Code: To install Claude Code, use the official Anthropic installer. To do that, open Terminal on your Mac and paste this command: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
Wait a few minutes, and then you will see a ” Claude Code successfully installed message in your terminal.
Check the setup notes below. If you see something like installation exists but ~/.local/bin is not in your PATH, it means the terminal still can’t find Claude Code yet.
Now follow the next two steps. If you don’t see such a note, you can quit the terminal, reopen it, and use this command to confirm that Claude Code has been successfully installed on your device: confirm claude –version. If you see a Claude version, it’s installed on your device. Then continue with part two.
Next, paste this command into the terminal and press Enter: echo ‘export PATH=”$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH”‘ >> ~/.zshrc
Next, paste this: source ~/.zshrc, and press Enter. Now type claude –version and press Enter. You will see the Claude version number. This means Claude Code is successfully installed on your device in the terminal
Part 2: Turn on Claude access in Edits
Next, you need to let Claude access your Instagram edits apps. First, ensure the Instagram edits app is installed on your Mac. If not, you can use the official download link here. Once installed, follow the steps below:
Step 1: Open the app on your Mac and sign in with your account. On the home screen, you will go directly to the Projects tab.
Step 2: Next, you can tap on your profile picture in the top right corner of the screen or click on the edit option in the menu bar at the top of the screen and then click on the settings
Step 3: Next, tap on the automation from the sidebar
Step 4: By default, automation is turned off. Now, from the automation settings, turn on the toggle that says Enable Automation Server.
Step 5: Under the Connect an AI Client section, click the copy icon next to the Claude code. This will copy the connection command with your access token. Remember, don’t share this command with others. In this case, I am using Claude code. If you are using Codex, tap the copy button next to Codex. The same goes for Muse.
You can also connect any AI model. Since it is a standard MCP server, any AI app can connect to the MCP server over HTTPS and can control edits.
Remember to replace <TOKEN> with the Access token from Edits > Settings > Automation, and keep Edits open with the automation server turned on
For Google Gemini CLI:
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli
gemini mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp
For Qwen:
npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code
qwen mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp
For DeepSeek, Grok, Mistral, Kimi, GLM, and most others, we can use OpenCode
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
{
“$schema”: “https://opencode.ai/config.json”,
“mcp”: {
“servers”: {
“edits”: {
“type”: “remote”,
“url”: “http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp”,

“headers”: { “Authorization”: “Bearer <TOKEN>” }
}
}
}
}
Part 3: Connect Claude Code to Edits
Next, let’s connect Claude Code (or any AI model) to edits. Remember that you can only do this once.
Step 1: Now, paste the command you copied from the previous section into the terminal. You will see: Added HTTP MCP server metapilot-native
Step 2: Next, for Claude, paste this command: claude mcp get metapilot-native and press Enter. Under status, if you see Connected, it worked. If it says Failed to connect, ensure the edits app is running and follow the previous steps carefully.
For other models, follow these:
| App (models) | Connect command | Check it worked | 
| Claude Code (Claude) | claude mcp add –transport http –scope user metapilot-native http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” | claude mcp get metapilot-native | 
| Gemini CLI (Gemini) | gemini mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp | gemini mcp list | 
| Qwen Code (Qwen) | qwen mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp | qwen mcp list | 
| Codex (OpenAI GPT) | echo ‘export EDITS_TOKEN=”<TOKEN>”‘ >> ~/.zshrc && source ~/.zshrc && codex mcp add edits –url http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp –bearer-token-env-var EDITS_TOKEN | Run codex, then type /mcp | 
| OpenCode (DeepSeek, Grok, Mistral, Kimi, GLM and more) | No command. Paste the opencode.jsonc block from my last message into the folder you run OpenCode in. | opencode mcp list | 
| LM Studio (local Llama, Gemma, Qwen, DeepSeek R1) | No command. Program tab, then Install, then Edit mcp.json, and paste the JSON block. | Look at the Program tab | 
| Cursor (any model it offers) | No command. Paste the same JSON into ~/.cursor/mcp.json. | Cursor Settings, then MCP | 
Part 4: Start Claude Code
Now go to the folder where the videos are saved to edit them using Instagram edits. I recommend that you store all the videos in the Movies folder so it is easy to access in the future. In this case, I stored all my files in the Movies folder on my Mac. Now, once you have access to the folder, follow the steps below.
Step 1: To use Claude, go to the folder using the CD command. For example: cd ~/Downloads or cd ~/Movies. In my case, cd ~/Movies. Next, once you are in the folder, Type Cluade and press Return.
Step 2: Claude will ask whether you trust the folder you provided. Use the down arrow and select I trust this folder, and press Enter. It asks only once, and once you give permission, you can store all future videos in this folder for edits.
Step 3: To check, you can type /mcp and press Enter. It lists the apps Claude Code is connected to. metapilot-native with a green tick means Claude can control Edits.
Step 4: Go to the metapilot-native option and press Enter to see more details. You can use the down or up arrow to navigate between the options.
Part 5: Make your first Reel with Claude
Now let’s use Claude to create my first reel. In this case, I asked Claude to edit a 50-second coffee reel from five clips. In your case, you can store all the clips in the folder. First, test the connection again. Once done, follow the steps below.
To test the connection, go to your folder and type list my Instagram edits projects and press Enter. You will see metabolist native and the table of all your edit projects.
Step 2 : Now you can ask Claude to make edits for the Instagram reel video. You can manually create a new project, add clips, and point Claude to the project title and edit your videos, or you can ask Claude to create a project, add clips, and edit your first reel. I recommend giving Claude the full location of your clips and the title.
Step 3: That’s it. Claude will now create a new project and add Sunclips. You can open the Instagram Edits app to see the changes.
Step 4: Once you’ve loaded the clips, you can ask Claude to add transitions between them and also add titles, sound effects, and much more. In this case, I’m asking Claude to add the title “Morning Coffee” in big white text for two seconds and then add smooth transitions between the clips.
Step 5: Once you’ve made the edits, you can also ask Claude Core to export the clips in 4K, and it does it for you.
Step 6: Once the video is exported, Claude notifies you of the length, format, and size. You can open the same folder to see the clip. Claude also notifies you where the clip is stored and its title.
Let AI Handle Your Video Editing
This is how to connect Claude code using Instagram Edits MCP. For now, the Instagram Edits app is only available on macOS, and you can connect any AI model to make edits.
Since Claude requires a subscription, you can try a free AI model if you have one. You can also run any free AI model locally and ask it to edit, but the quality may vary and may not be as good as frontend models.
Since this guide focuses entirely on Claude Code, we are also creating a separate guide on how to connect other free AI models, including Google Gemini (which comes with a free Jio AI offer), DeepSeek, and other models.
If you have any issues while connecting Claude Code, let me know. If you prefer a video guide, we have also created one that you can check out above.

Nvidia stock extended its pre-market decline after the company announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as chief executive.

New Delhi- The Union Home Ministry on Friday extended the ban on controversial preacher Zakir Naik’s Islamic Research Foundation for another five years, noting it has been indulging in activities that are prejudicial to the security of the country and have the potential to disturb peace and communal harmony.
The ministry had invoked the powers conferred by Sub-section (1) of Section 3 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (37 of 1967), to declare the IRF as an unlawful association, which was upheld by the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Tribunal, it said in a gazette notification.
The earlier ban was ending on November 14.
“The Central Government is of the opinion that the IRF and its members, particularly the founder and President of the IRF, Dr Zakir Abdul Karim Naik alias Dr Zakir Naik, has been encouraging and aiding its followers to promote or attempt to promote, on grounds of religion, disharmony or feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious communities and groups which are prejudicial to the integrity and security of the country,” it said.
The statements and speeches made by Naik are objectionable and subversive and he has been promoting enmity and hatred amongst different religious groups and inspiring youths of a particular religion in India and abroad to commit terrorist acts, it said.
Naik made radical statements and speeches to millions of people worldwide through international satellite TV networks, Internet, print and social media, it said.
If the unlawful activities of the IRF are not curbed and controlled immediately, it will continue its subversive activities and re-organise its activists, who are still absconding, disrupt the secular fabric of the country by polluting the minds of the people by creating communal disharmony and propagate anti-national sentiments, it said.
The ministry said the outfit will escalate secessionism by supporting militancy and undertake activities which are prejudicial to the sovereignty, integrity and security of the country, it said.
“The central government, for the above-mentioned reasons, is of the opinion that having regard to the activities of the IRF, it is necessary to declare the IRF as an unlawful association with immediate effect,” it said.

Ukraine's Starlink problems are back, it said on Thursday.
Troops and officials said their access to Starshield, the military version of Starlink, has been curbed once again to a 100-mph speed limit, severely disrupting war operations such as air defense and strikes in Russia's rear.
It's the second time that Kyiv has reported a major disruption to the service, coming about three weeks after Ukraine said it suffered a 10-day slowdown under a similar speed limit.
"The speed limit is back at 161 kilometers per hour. That's 100 miles per hour," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said at a summit in Dublin.
He added that Ukraine's interceptor drones, which it relies on to counter jet-powered loitering munitions near the front lines, couldn't maintain a connection while flying at speeds fast enough to catch their targets.
"This means more Russian strikes get through, and more of our people are killed by Russia. We are trying to get the details from the American side, but so far, we know very little," Zelenskyy said.
A spokesperson for SpaceX denied the disruption in comments to several international media outlets, saying: "This is false. There has been no change."
SpaceX and the Pentagon did not respond to comment requests sent outside regular business hours by Business Insider.
Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov, an advisor to Zelenskyy's office on drones, wrote on his Telegram channel that communications had also been disrupted for helicopters tasked with chasing and shooting down Russian jet drones — another key pillar of its air defense.
"We did not rejoice for long," he said of the initial resumption of Starshield services, which happened in mid-October.
Zelenskyy said in a separate post on his Telegram channel that Ukrainian forces had been "reporting significant failures" with Starshield for several days, particularly near the front lines or in Russian-occupied territories.
"Unfortunately, strikes have already gotten through because interception systems cannot reach sufficient speed in time to catch them," he said.
"The Ukrainian military has already checked the circumstances of this, and these are not random errors, but a system speed limit," Zelenskyy added.
The Financial Times reported that several unnamed senior Ukrainian officials suspected the speed limit was related to the US putting pressure on Kyiv amid this week's peace talks in Abu Dhabi, and as US envoys flew to Russia to meet with its leader, Vladimir Putin, on Thursday.
Why Starshield matters for the war
Ukrainian troops and civilians alike rely heavily on Starlink for communications, but Kyiv's forces say they equip their medium-range strike drones and interceptors with terminals that link to Starshield, which is controlled by the US government.
Most commercial Starlink terminals officially stop working at a maximum speed of 100 mph, meaning Ukrainian drones flying faster typically need Starshield to stay connected.
When Ukraine's Starshield access was previously disrupted, it said it had tested connections outside its territory and found that the speed limit was only imposed within its borders.
Zelenskyy had publicly called on SpaceX owner Elon Musk and President Donald Trump for answers about the slowdown, but both have said they were not responsible.
Musk, however, had accused Ukraine of breaching Starlink's terms of service by using the service in attack drones. Ukrainian military figures, including Beskrestnov, have denied the claim.

Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.
To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.
Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.
This year, Jarnecki has written about Iran’s drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the broader implications for governments and Big Tech. He has also commented on the impacts of Russia and Ukraine exchanging strikes on each other’s data centers.

As telescopes go, few if any are more famous than the Hubble Space Telescope. Over 30 years of operations, the telescope has been essential to groundbreaking discoveries that have fundamentally transformed humanity’s view of the universe. But like all satellites in low Earth orbit, it’s been gradually descending.
This happens because of atmospheric drag, and the Hubble Space Telescope is not equipped with a propulsion system to adjust its own orbit. According to NASA’s analysis, if left unchecked, the telescope will likely re-enter Earth’s atmosphere in 2033 or 2034, eventually crashing back onto the planet.
Hoping to delay this conclusion, NASA has issued a formal Request for Information seeking proposals from the private sector for “in-space servicing” of the famous telescope. This would likely involve raising Hubble’s altitude to extend its operational lifespan, but the agency is also open to industry’s suggestions for managing a safe and controlled reentry or disposal of the telescope while still in orbit. Space companies can also propose upgrades to enhance the telescope’s functionality in its remaining years.
“Hubble is a national icon,” Nicky Fox, associate administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate, said in a statement. “Given the time we have until Hubble’s anticipated reentry, we are eager to explore the breadth of possibilities to boost Hubble to a higher orbit while we develop the flagship mission to follow.”
The telescope was designed with the expectation that astronauts would perform repairs and upgrades in orbit. Since it was launched in 1990, a total of five service missions have been carried out. The last of these missions was canceled after the space shuttle Columbia disaster in 2003. But NASA later determined that the benefits of servicing Hubble outweighed the risks of a final mission, and in 2009 a crew took measures, such as replacing the battery, to extend the telescope’s lifespan.
This is also not the first time NASA has considered private-sector resources for raising the Hubble Space Telescope’s orbit. In September 2022, NASA entered into a nonfunding partnership agreement with SpaceX to investigate the possibility of using the company’s Dragon spacecraft to move Hubble into a more stable orbit. However, according to NASA’s announcement at the time, the agency had no plans to conduct or fund the service mission itself; the study was intended solely to assess commercial feasibility.
Meanwhile, NASA commissioned the private company Katalyst Space Technologies in September 2025 to perform an orbital raise for the Swift Observatory, which was experiencing faster-than-expected orbital decay. However, the company’s spacecraft, launched in July 2026, suffered an attitude control malfunction, forcing the mission to be abandoned. On November 4, Swift reentered the atmosphere over Indonesia.
The problems facing the Hubble Space Telescope are not limited to its drop in altitude. The spacecraft itself is also experiencing malfunctions. In June 2024, NASA announced that it would transition the Hubble Space Telescope to a new operating mode using only one of the six gyros on board to assess the telescope’s orientation. After more than three decades in space, only three of the gyros were operational, and one of those was starting to return abnormal readings. The other remaining functional gyro is now being kept in a ready state for future use.
NASA estimates that a mission to raise the telescope’s orbit will need to be carried out by 2032. In an announcement made in 2022, NASA also explained that if the Hubble Space Telescope could be raised to a higher, more stable orbit, it could continue to observe the cosmos for several more years.
“Hubble still has important science ahead of it, and we should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible,” said NASA administrator Jared Isaacman. “If there are innovative and cost-effective ways to extend the life of an asset already in orbit, we owe it to the American taxpayer and the scientific community to explore them. Extending Hubble’s life would mean more discoveries, more science, and more opportunities to expand our understanding of the universe.”

Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen. These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen’s purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google’s ecosystem use.
With Google’s recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company’s products.
Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it’s 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces “fabricated claims” by more than 5x, according to Google’s analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash’s score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. Online travel aggregator (OTA) Yatra swung to the red and reported a consolidated net loss of ₹78.4 Lakhs in the second quarter (Q2) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27). In contrast, the travel tech platform has reported a net profit of ₹14.3 Cr in Q2 FY26 and ₹33.9 Lakhs in Q1 FY27. The losses came despite the company raking in ₹1.7 Cr in one-time deferred tax benefits during the quarter. The bottom line was primarily impacted as the company’s revenue from operations tanked 39.1% to ₹213.6 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹350.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. However, on a sequential basis, Yatra’s top line rose 13.7% from ₹187.9 Cr in the preceding quarter. The OTA attributed the losses to the “challenging operating environment”, lower MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions) volumes, and the reorientation of the MICE vertical towards smaller corporate group programmes. “... Our year-on-year profitability was impacted primarily by MICE, which faced an exceptionally strong comparable quarter last year and a tactical shift towards smaller corporate group programmes amid prevailing uncertainty…,” said Yatra CEO Siddhartha Gupta. Including other income of ₹4.4 Cr, Yatra’s total income stood at ₹218 Cr in Q2 FY27. Meanwhile, total expenses for the quarter under review declined 35% to ₹219.9 Cr compared to ₹339 Cr in Q2 FY26. The company also incurred an additional tax expense of ₹59.3 Lakh during the quarter. Revenue less service cost (RLSC), which is essentially the gross margin, declined 0.2% to ₹125.5 Cr in Q2 FY27. As a result, EBITDA declined 47% YoY to ₹13.2 Cr, while EBITDA margin stood at 10.48%during the quarter under review. In a statement, the company’s gross bookings grew 6% YoY and 3% QoQ to ₹2,165.5 Cr in Q2 FY27. During the quarter, Yatra said that it added 54 new corporate customers with an estimated annual revenue potential of ₹203.5 Cr. “We continue to make progress on our strategic priorities, including expanding into the SME and mid-market segments through Travel Pro, strengthening our expense management offering through RECAP, expanding hotel supply and leveraging AI-led automation. These initiatives are helping us broaden our addressable market and build a more scalable business, positioning us for sustainable growth and improved profitability over the medium term,” added Gupta. Yatra’s US Entity On Nasdaq’s Radar Separately, the travel tech platform’s US-listed entity, Yatra Online Inc, said that it has received a letter from Nasdaq after its shares traded below the exchange’s minimum $1 closing bid price for more than a month. This has effectively put the travel tech company on a compliance watch. The company said that the notice does not immediately delist the company’s shares from the Nasdaq Capital Market. However, the OTA said that it has been given a timeline of 180 days, until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance. To do so, its shares must close at $1 or higher for at least 10 consecutive business days, even though Nasdaq may require up to 20 consecutive days in certain cases. If Yatra fails to meet the requirement by May next year, it may qualify for an additional 180-day compliance period. This would require the company to meet Nasdaq’s other continued-listing thresholds and formally notify the exchange of its intention to cure the deficiency. A reverse stock split is among the options available to lift the share price. Yatra said it may consider such a move if necessary, but cautioned that there is no assurance it will regain compliance. Nevertheless, Yatra said it intends to closely monitor its closing bid price and may evaluate available options to restore compliance. The notice highlights the pressure facing the travel-tech company’s US-listed shares. As of 1:13 AM IST, shares of Yatra Online Inc were trading at $0.77, down 18% in the past six months and nearly 57% lower on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. This comes as the US-listed Yatra Online Inc has been reporting increased net losses, compressed margins and falling revenues. Slowing growth in core verticals, market volatility and rising short-term trade-related borrowings have further led to the sell-off in the stock. But a sustained share price below $1 can further reduce liquidity, deter institutional investors and complicate future fundraising. Meanwhile, shares of India-listed Yatra closed Thursday’s trading session 0.94% lower at ₹81.03 on the BSE.

Failed health check, elevated load, server restart: What led to the Microsoft outage
Automated server shutdowns created an infrastructure bottleneck, even as engineers deploy alternatives, while an initial fix attempt don’t seem to be delivering results
Microsoft services, including Microsoft 365 for Business and Enterprise, as well as consumer products such as Microsoft Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and Office on the web, continue to experience what the tech company described as a “service degradation” following a major global outage that has stretched across several hours.
Microsoft has yet to confirm why the services went offline in the early hours of Friday, but it attributes the outage to several servers unexpectedly becoming unavailable after failing automated health checks, which placed elevated strain on the remaining infrastructure worldwide.
The Microsoft Service Health Status currently lists all customer services as “operational”, but Microsoft’s update on X indicated there were issues to resolve.
Deep Dive
“We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they’re not taking as expected. We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances,” said Microsoft 365 Status account on X.
Why the services went offline
By all accounts, the outage was caused by a cascading infrastructure failure.
It began with automated health checks across its server infrastructure, which failed on certain servers and caused them to shut down. This increased the load on the remaining online servers, causing a cascading effect. Microsoft engineers have attempted to restart these servers, and Microsoft 365 Status does indicate that a portion of the affected servers has been restarted and remains stable.
Restarting a server requires as long as 30 minutes, depending on hardware and workload. After an unexpected crash or hard reboot, the server may run a disk check process, which can take a long time on large drives. There is no guarantee that the issue which caused the server to shut down or become unresponsive will be fixed by a restart.
“We’re testing a configuration change to address a problem that’s causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable,” Microsoft said before it started deploying certain fixes. That attempt hasn’t delivered results so far.
Microsoft said the disruption wasn’t driven by a spike in user traffic or a cyberattack. Instead, a core process on affected servers became overwhelmed, causing capacity loss when servers failed automated health checks and dropped offline. As a result, services became unavailable and unstable.

“Fifty-seven channels, and nothin’ on.”
Bruce Springsteen famously said those words during a concert and later in a song in the 1990s about the number of TV channels seemingly growing disproportionately to the availability of enjoyable content.
Within a few years, there would be hundreds of TV channels and still, some would argue in hyperbolic frustration, “nothing to watch.”
The advent of streaming services was poised as a potential solution to this problem. It granted viewers easy, on-demand access to thousands of movies and shows, which, theoretically, could ensure that viewers could always find something to watch.
According to a survey from Nielsen’s Gracenote, though, that’s not exactly the case today.
Gracenote, a Nielsen-owned content data business, surveyed 3,000 video streaming users in the US, Brazil, France, Germany, Mexico, and the UK who were at least 18 years old for its “2026 State of Play: Amid fragmentation frustrations, UX is the future of streaming” report. It found that many struggle to find something to stream. However, this is not necessarily because there’s nothing good on, but rather because they find it difficult to home in on good content on streaming services.
For example, over 51 percent of respondents said that “the abundance of content and [streaming] services is making it harder to find something to watch.”
Further, 19.2 percent of respondents said that, on average, they either “always” or “often” don’t know what to watch, can’t find anything, and then decide to do something else. And 27.4 percent of respondents said that, on average, they either always or often try to watch a specific program but end up not watching it because they couldn’t find it on streaming.
“Through the lens of catalogue size and streaming usage, connecting the 83.4 percent who don’t always know what they want to watch should be fairly straightforward, especially as companies increasingly use customer data to create personalized experiences that foster long-term engagement and loyalty. Audiences, however, aren’t finding what they’re looking for, and content discovery challenges are mounting,” the report reads.

Would you cancel a trip because it falls on Friday the 13th? For some people, the date brings more than a passing worry. It can trigger intense fear even when there is no clear danger. That fear has a name that may be harder to face than the calendar itself. It is called paraskevidekatriaphobia. The word comes from three Greek terms. Paraskevi means Friday, dekatria means thirteen, and phobia means fear. Another name for the same fear is friggatriskaidekaphobia. The fear of the number 13 alone is called triskaidekaphobia. Say it slowly as par-uh-SKEE-vuh-dek-uh-TRY-uh-foh-bee-uh. Psychotherapist Donald Dossey helped popularise the term. He joked that once you could pronounce it, you were cured. Getting the syllables right may earn a laugh. For someone whose fear disrupts daily life, treatment can help. A person may feel anxious just thinking about the date. Even seeing the date on a calendar can bring on symptoms. Others may panic as the day approaches. Their heart may race, and they may sweat or feel sick. Some people may also feel dizzy or struggle to catch their breath. Fear can influence ordinary decisions, too. Someone might postpone a journey, put off signing a contract or cancel dinner plans. Some people arrange their work around the date to avoid meetings or important decisions altogether. Others might stay home to avoid anything they believe could bring bad luck. How much this fear disrupts daily life matters more than any one symptom. A doctor or mental health professional can assess persistent fear and its effects. The exact origin remains uncertain. One Christian tradition connects the number 13 with the Last Supper. It identifies Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus Christ, as the 13th guest. Friday also carries its own associations, including the crucifixion of Jesus. Another story links the date to the arrest of the Knights Templar. The arrests began in France on Friday, October 13, 1307. The link to today's superstition remains uncertain. Research generally finds Friday the 13th is about as unlucky as any other day. Friday the 13th occurs three times in 2026. The first two fell in February and March. November 13 is the last one this year. If the fear regularly changes your plans, a mental health professional can help. One common treatment for specific phobias is exposure therapy. It involves gradually facing what you fear with guidance. The aim is to reduce the fear and help you return to your usual activities. How Riley went from KSI's trainer to world-title dream
- Published
Viddal Riley had spent years learning how to fight. Then he taught a YouTuber, and that became the story.
On Saturday, the Londoner defends his European cruiserweight title against unbeaten Frenchman Seydi Coupe at Wembley Arena, with a world-title shot within reach.
Yet it was his work with social media star KSI that first brought him mainstream attention, training the YouTuber for his fights against Joe Weller and Logan Paul.
From a corner of boxing where popularity can secure a headline fight before a punch has been thrown, Riley, 29, arrived with credentials few of his new audience knew about.
"I didn't do all that hard work from such a young age to just be known as a trainer of a famous person," he tells BBC Sport.
"I can't push away something that's part of my story. I just wanted to make sure that's not the only thing I'm known as and I've managed to do that."
Riley, unbeaten in 14 professional fights, first entered a boxing gym aged six and was national champion at 11.
He collected eight titles in the amateurs, representing Team GB and captaining England before meeting KSI at 19.
English, British and European titles have followed as a professional. He thought beating Cheavon Clarke might win over the sceptics, but the influencer tag has proved hard to shift.
"I'm pretty much giving up on trying to convince a purist of what I am," he says. "If you can't read facts and figures to convince yourself, then you're in your own world."
From a YouTuber trainer to Mayweather and Mexico
When Riley went to Las Vegas as KSI's trainer, he made sure his own boxing kit was in the luggage. The trip came about because Floyd Mayweather Sr wanted to build his social media presence.
"I took it as an opportunity to showcase my abilities even though I was there as his trainer," he says.
Riley - who had already made his professional debut in Tijuana, Mexico in 2018 - sparred with established professionals and impressed enough to earn a deal with Mayweather Promotions the following year.
There had been moments, though, when Riley wondered whether life as a cornerman might suit him better.
"Seeing how they were living and how I could not be the one in danger and still make a good life for myself, it does make you second guess," he says.
But Riley wanted to pursue his own career. His first professional appearance in Britain would not come until his fifth fight.
Joining MF Pro - 'there's no loophole, there's no life hack'
Working with KSI taught Riley how to handle the media glare. He built an audience of his own and now has about 1.2 million YouTube subscribers.
"It got me accustomed to being in the limelight," he says. "Ready for the attention to be on me on a big stage."
After starting with Mayweather Promotions, Riley developed his career with Boxxer - winning English and British titles.
His points victory over Clarke looks better still after Clarke stopped former world champion Chris Billam-Smith last weekend.
"Some things take time to mature," Riley says. "It allows people to understand the level that I am and my capabilities."
Yet joining MF Pro in December 2025 risked bringing the conversation back to influencer boxing. Before signing with the professional venture affiliated with KSI's Misfits, Riley wanted the distinction made clear.
"Are you going to make this clear that I'm not joining Misfits Boxing?" he recalls asking. "I haven't done all of this hard work to then sign a professional contract that's going to drag me back into what I've worked so hard to differentiate myself from."
Riley says he had offers from "basically all promoters", but felt MF Pro best appreciated both his boxing and his audience. Assurances he could continue pursuing a world title made signing "a no-brainer".
He believes other fighters can learn from his approach, but warns against expecting a shortcut: "You can't skip anything. There's no loophole, there's no life hack or anything like that."
When will Riley get a world-title shot?
Victory over Mateusz Masternak secured an IBF mandatory position, with New Zealand's David Nyika lined up to face Riley for the vacant title. Those plans are being held up by former champion Jai Opetaia's legal dispute with the governing body.
The IBF stripped Opetaia after he fought Brandon Glanton despite it withdrawing approval for the bout. The Australian is challenging that decision while also stepping up to heavyweight to face Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua undercard in December.
"It's messy up there right now, but I'm trying to get in the mess," Riley says.
Rather than wait, he has opted to defend his European belt against Coupe, also unbeaten in 14 fights. He will not predict when his world-title opportunity might arrive.
"I'm just hyper-focused on Saturday. I can't go past Saturday," he says. "In my mind, the world ends on Saturday."
One name persuades him to look beyond it. Oleksandr Usyk, whose team say he is considering returning to cruiserweight, would be Riley's dream opponent.
"Much respect to him - he's a legend," he says. "But to be able to step in the ring with him and battle, that will be sick."

Meta's Muse can now make calls on your behalf (if you have a paid subscription)
The AI agent can schedule appointments, make reservations and wait on hold for you.
Meta's Muse just got another ability that could make the AI agent feel a little bit more like an actual personal assistant. Muse is now able to place phone calls on your behalf, if you have a paid subscription.
With the change, Muse is able to call businesses to help with tasks like making reservations, scheduling appointments and other "calls you don't want to make," Meta's Chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said in an update. The feature is available to those who have paid for a separate Muse subscription, which comes with additional tokens and some extra features.
Some users who have had access to the feature already have reported that Muse has been able to handle phone-related tasks with relative ease. Moltbook creator and Meta Superintelligence employee Matt Schlicht shared a recreation of a phone conversation his agent had with a Volvo dealership last month, noting that it was able to wait on hold in order to get the info he needed.
My muse called Volvo for me to see when the next available appointment is.
You can listen to the phone call here.
I have it do multiple calls like this every day (I'm still trying to get better and better at leveraging muse).
My muse called, waited on the line for 15 minutes,... pic.twitter.com/bosH1tyW1R

Interestingly, in the call shared by Schlicht, Muse doesn't explicitly identify itself as an AI agent though it notes it's calling his behalf and that it's transcribing the call. Rwanda's army team removed from Africa league after US sanctions, NBA says
- Published
The National Basketball Association (NBA) says it removed Rwanda's army team from its African league because of US sanctions imposed on the country in March.
The NBA had previously said the Rwandan army-funded Armée Patriotique Rwandaise (APR) club would not participate in the 2026 Basketball Africa League (BAL).
However this is the first time the NBA has revealed the reasons behind the APR's removal.
The association was responding to complaints by two US senators, who sent a letter asking them to reconsider their partnership with the Rwandan team. The US placed sanctions on the Rwandan army, accusing it of fuelling the conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo in March.
The senators said the NBA risked "becoming complicit in sportswashing by accepting money from a Rwandan government that systematically abuses human rights".
Last week, the US also imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its support for the M23 rebel group which has seized control of large parts of eastern DR Congo. Rwanda denies backing the rebels despite overwhelming evidence.
Rwanda is an official BAL partner and pays the league to host its finals at the 10,000-seat BK Arena in the capital, Kigali.
The BBC has asked Rwanda for comment.

In the letter to the NBA dated 23 October, Democratic Senator Jeffrey Merkley and Republican counterpart Marsha Blackburn gave the association until 2 November to give a written response regarding its continued partnership with Rwanda.

Among other queries, they also questioned how the association could "reconcile its continued partnership with Rwanda with its purported commitment to justice".
In its response, NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said the Rwandan team "had been withdrawn" from the BAL following the sanctions imposed earlier in the year, American sports website ESPN reports.

ChatGPT maker OpenAI has introduced local inference and data processing for its APIs in India, adding to its efforts to expand the commercialisation of ChatGPT in its largest market. For context, local data inferencing allows businesses to ensure that both API requests and the computing required to generate responses take place within India for supported workloads. It is initially available for the GPT-6 Luna model and extends OpenAI's existing data residency options in the country. OpenAI's India enterprise head Nitin Bawankule pointed out that local inference gives businesses greater control over where their data is processed and could help more organisations move from experimenting with AI to deploying it in their day-to-day operations. "Some Indian businesses have not fully deployed AI for important work because they need the information involved to be processed within the country," Bawankule said. To use the new offering, customers need to create a new API project, select India as the location for both data storage and processing, and use the corresponding India regional endpoint. With the launch, India joins Australia and Japan as the latest markets where OpenAI has introduced API inference residency. Global AI Giants Push For Data Localisation In India Data localisation has emerged as an important consideration in enterprise AI adoption. While global AI models offer advanced capabilities, businesses handling sensitive information require a greater understanding of where their data is going. Storage and processing of data before model deployment is something that cannot be compromised from a security perspective for banks, financial institutions and government agencies. For these clients, data residency and infrastructure requirements can limit the use of international frontier AI models in production environments. OpenAI is not the first international AI company looking to address India's data localisation requirements. In August, Anthropic announced plans to bring in-country inference for its Claude AI models to India through Amazon Bedrock, AWS' managed service for building generative AI applications. The move was aimed at addressing data residency and infrastructure requirements that have kept banks, financial institutions and government agencies from deploying international AI models in production. Anthropic has since made similar data residency capabilities available for certain models on AWS Bedrock. For Indian AI startups such as Sarvam AI, locally hosted inference has also been an important differentiator when competing with global AI players. However, the entry of OpenAI and Anthropic into this segment could narrow that advantage as international companies begin offering similar capabilities in the country. For OpenAI, data inferencing is another piece of its India revenue. The AI giant has established a strong hold on the Indian market, where more than 10 Cr people interact with ChatGPT on a weekly basis. The company is looking to monetise its India holding. OpenAI Expands Its Business Offering On ChatGPT In a bid to deepen its engagement with businesses, OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT, a beta offering that allows businesses to claim and manage their profiles through a new Business Hub. Companies can update their information, add product feeds and access aggregated insights into how users discover and engage with them on ChatGPT. These insights include business mentions, website clicks and discovery topics across conversations where their websites are cited. OpenAI has also introduced Business Agents, which allow customers to interact with businesses, explore their offerings and ask product-related questions directly within ChatGPT. However, the feature is initially available only to eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the US. Businesses in markets where ChatGPT is available, including India, can claim their profiles through Business Hub, subject to eligibility and verification requirements. OpenAI's broader efforts to expand its presence in India include investments and partnerships to develop domestic AI infrastructure. Earlier this year, the company partnered with Tata Group to develop domestic AI data centre capacity. It has also extended data residency capabilities for certain models through AWS Bedrock.
